a64.speaker: Bamory Kamagaté, Director General of the École normale supérieure (Ens), Côte d'Ivoire
a64.name: Bamory Kamagaté
a64.title: Director General of the École normale supérieure (Ens), Côte d'Ivoire
a64.speech: Said that alongside the rehabilitated and equipped laboratories, four rooms equipped with 25 computers each were also received, three at the Ens and one at the Jean Piaget application school. Said "A fifth, larger room is equipped with 45 interconnected desktop computers and a Vestel [interactive display]. In addition to all this, we also have laptops, electronic tablets, video projectors, cameras and multifunction printers, to name just a few." Recalled that this important equipment will help improve the quality of teaching, learner training, and research activities. Recalled that another important component of the collaboration with Mca-CI concerns the construction and equipping of Ens branches in San Pedro and Bouaké. Said "The next step will be to carefully consider the choice of application schools that will support these branches. The idea is to rely either on the schools of excellence built precisely by the Mca in these two regions, or on the public institutions located there. On this matter, an imminent meeting is planned between Mca-CI and Ens experts. A report will be submitted to the minister following this meeting."

a64.speaker: Adama Diawara, Ivorian Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research
a64.name: Adama Diawara
a64.title: Ivorian Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research
a64.speech: Expressed satisfaction at the successful completion of the rehabilitation and equipping of the school with scientific and educational material by the Mcc and the Mca. Noted that this donation is only part of the broader Employability and Productivity Project (155 million USD) aimed at improving the employability of Ivorians and the productivity of the private sector by improving the quality, supply and access to technical and basic skills, in response to private sector demand. Said "We remain convinced that this will significantly improve the working conditions and quality of training at this school, whose primary mission is to train the trainers of our education system."

a108.speaker: Larry Madowo, CNN journalist
a108.name: Larry Madowo
a108.title: CNN journalist
a108.speech: Highlighted the crisis unfolding in Africa with a report on a Ugandan HIV/AIDS patient who lost access to life-saving medication following the withdrawal of USAID funding ; has already warned that the withdrawal of USAID funding could have devastating consequences for those who depend on it.

a108.speaker: Scott Perry, U.S. Congressman
a108.name: Scott Perry
a108.title: U.S. Congressman
a108.speech: In a congressional briefing, exposed USAID's operations, suggesting that its activities may rival or even surpass those of the CIA during the Cold War, when global influence was contested between the U.S. and the now-defunct Soviet Union.

a108.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a108.name: Donald Trump
a108.title: U.S. President
a108.speech: Claimed that USAID had "strayed from its original mission of responsibly advancing interests abroad."

a108.speaker: Ali Ndume, Nigerian Senator for Borno State
a108.name: Ali Ndume
a108.title: Nigerian Senator for Borno State
a108.speech: Has called for further scrutiny, following claims that USAID funds may have indirectly benefited terrorist groups.

a108.speaker: Dr. Dambisa Moyo, economist, in her book 'Dead Aid: Why Aid is Not Working and How There is a Better Way for Africa'
a108.name: Dr. Dambisa Moyo
a108.title: economist, in her book 'Dead Aid: Why Aid is Not Working and How There is a Better Way for Africa'
a108.speech: Made the case that foreign aid rarely helps its intended recipients.

a108.speaker: Magnus Onyibe, master's thesis at Tufts University's Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, 'Darfur: Why the West Failed to Help'
a108.name: Magnus Onyibe
a108.title: master's thesis at Tufts University's Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, 'Darfur: Why the West Failed to Help'
a108.speech: Analysed global conflicts over the past century, tracing how competition for natural resources, dating back to the Rockefeller and Rothschild families' dominance in the oil industry, fuelled international crises, one of the most devastating consequences being the 1915 Armenian genocide, reportedly carried out under the influence of these powerful industrialists.

a196.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.name: Zurab Pololikashvili
a196.title: United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.speech: Stresses: “Strengthening multilateralism through tourism will deliver results in socio-economic inclusion, sustainable development, peace and understanding.” ; Addressing G20 Tourism Ministers, he commended the South African Presidency’s focus on inclusion and sustainability: “More than a motto, the theme for South Africa’s G20 Presidency ‘solidarity, equality, sustainability’, reminds us that Equality and Sustainability can only be achieved through targeted policies, unified efforts and mutual support among countries – a recognition that in an interconnected world, the challenges faced by one country can have ripple effects globally.”

a196.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.name: Zurab Pololikashvili
a196.title: United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.speech: Reaffirms the critical importance of progressing digital transformation, financing for development, investment and resilient ecosystems in tourism, stressing that there will be no resilience without sustainability ; Calls for supporting innovation and stressed that emerging technologies can transform tourism MSMEs, which are the backbone of tourism, but only with adequate financing and programmes to close the digital divide and promote inclusion.

a196.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.name: Zurab Pololikashvili
a196.title: United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.speech: Noted that though “for many developing countries, including Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States, tourism is a major source of employment, foreign exchange and tax revenues. Yet, the sector continues to be overlooked as a tool for development, with the total Official Development Assistance disbursements for tourism remaining below 0.11 per cent of total ODA.”

a196.speaker: Zurab Pololikashvili, United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.name: Zurab Pololikashvili
a196.title: United Nations (UN) Tourism Secretary General
a196.speech: Highlights South Africa’s G20 Presidency as a show of the continent’s leadership in the global agenda. He recalled that Africa is home to 19 per cent of the world’s population, with 70 per cent of sub-Saharan Africa under the age of 30. “The opportunities the continent offers in tourism are many” he said and “unlocking tourism investment and development for jobs and inclusion is a core priority of the UN Tourism Agenda for Africa.”

a196.speaker: World Tourism Barometer (report)
a196.name: World Tourism Barometer (report)
a196.speech: According to the latest World Tourism Barometer, international tourist arrivals increased 5 per cent in the first half of 2025.

a245.speaker: Chie-Bhol and Chie-Mankhoat communities of Akobo County (collective pledge)
a245.name: Chie-Bhol and Chie-Mankhoat communities of Akobo County (collective pledge)
a245.speech: During the commemoration, the communities pledged to embrace forgiveness, denounce revenge attacks, and stop composing or singing songs that incite hatred; they also resolved to allow free and safe movement between both sides, reinforcing their commitment to lasting peace.

a245.speaker: Deng Reat, youth leader from the Chie-Mankhoat subclan
a245.name: Deng Reat
a245.title: youth leader from the Chie-Mankhoat subclan
a245.speech: Emphasized the importance of peacebuilding and urged all to abandon any form of violence.

a245.speaker: Thijin Ruot, youth leader of the Chie-Bhol subclan
a245.name: Thijin Ruot
a245.title: youth leader of the Chie-Bhol subclan
a245.speech: Encouraged forgiveness and peaceful coexistence among the communities.

a245.speaker: Martha Nyachieng Chuol, an elderly woman
a245.name: Martha Nyachieng Chuol
a245.title: an elderly woman
a245.speech: Expressed her joy over the peace agreement, which brought an end to years of unrest and restored hope for a more peaceful future.

a248.speaker: Benin public television channel (Chaîne des grands événements)
a248.name: Benin public television channel (Chaîne des grands événements)
a248.speech: According to the same public channel, some people, including the Head of State himself, had reportedly become producers of "white gold" (cotton).

a248.speaker: Economic operators and political leaders
a248.name: Economic operators and political leaders
a248.speech: Denounced the demonisation, notably of the sale of adulterated petrol, as nothing but an admission of a lack of vision, in a country that shares nearly 500 kilometres of border with Nigeria.

a248.speaker: Sabai Katé, former Minister of Agriculture of Benin
a248.name: Sabai Katé
a248.title: former Minister of Agriculture of Benin
a248.speech: Meanwhile threw dust in the eyes of the population by sounding the trumpet of the rehabilitation of the oil palm sector.

a248.speaker: Patrice Talon, cotton magnate (interview on Radio France Internationale, November 2012)
a248.name: Patrice Talon
a248.title: cotton magnate (interview on Radio France Internationale, November 2012)
a248.speech: Cited as the source showing that Talon had proved himself in the cotton sector long before the Boni Yayi regime came to power with cotton money.

a248.speaker: Burkinabè press
a248.name: Burkinabè press
a248.speech: At one point judged that in Benin, cotton is grown on television.

a327.speaker: A research firm (unnamed)
a327.name: A research firm (unnamed)
a327.speech: Has said Zimbabwe’s financial sector is primed for mergers and acquisitions in 2021 amid indications that a majority of institutions are struggling to raise capital ; “Our research reveals that there…”

a374.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a374.name: Donald Trump
a374.title: President of the United States
a374.speech: Suggested on Tuesday, speaking to journalists aboard Air Force One, that he might not attend the upcoming G20 leaders' summit in South Africa, expressing strong criticism of South Africa and denouncing in particular its land reform policy and its diplomatic posture hostile to Israel: “I have a lot of disagreements with South Africa. Their policies are very bad,” while raising the possibility of being represented by a special envoy rather than attending in person.

a374.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a374.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a374.title: President of South Africa
a374.speech: Continues to argue for Trump's participation in the summit and vigorously defends his government's national policies, which include economic justice measures in favour of the black population and land reforms aimed at correcting inequalities inherited from apartheid; has systematically rejected the accusations of discrimination or genocide against white landowners.

a374.speaker: Washington (US government)
a374.name: Washington (US government)
a374.speech: Has repeatedly expressed its concerns about the potential impact of these reforms on the rights of white landowners.

a535.speaker: Alliance for Affordable Internet (A4AI)
a535.name: Alliance for Affordable Internet (A4AI)
a535.speech: Announced the following projects at the annual Forum of the Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation in Abuja: the Alliance will begin work in three or four countries before the end of 2013 and expand to at least twelve countries by the end of 2015; members have committed to a number of policy best practices that will guide international advocacy; and A4AI will publish an annual "affordability report", the first edition due in December 2013.

a535.speaker: ITU (International Telecommunication Union)
a535.name: ITU (International Telecommunication Union)
a535.speech: Cited as the source for the figure that two-thirds of the world's population still do not have Internet access.

a535.speaker: Sir Tim Berners-Lee, inventor of the Web and founder of the World Wide Web Foundation
a535.name: Sir Tim Berners-Lee
a535.title: inventor of the Web and founder of the World Wide Web Foundation
a535.speech: "The reason for the Alliance is very simple: the majority of the world's population is still not connected to the Internet, often for lack of means. Take the case of Mozambique: a recent study showed that using just 1 GB of data can sometimes cost an average inhabitant more than two months' salary." ; "One of the consequences of these high prices is that the digital divide tends to widen and it slows progress in areas as vital as health, education and science. With the advent of affordable smartphones, new undersea cables and innovations in wireless networks, there is no longer any valid reason for this digital divide to persist. The real difficulty now is anti-competitive policies and regulation that imposes unaffordable prices. The Alliance is here to remove that obstacle and to help a great many people gain access to the Internet at an affordable price."

a535.speaker: Dr Bitange Ndemo, honorary president of A4AI and former permanent secretary of Kenya's Ministry of Information and Communications
a535.name: Dr Bitange Ndemo
a535.title: honorary president of A4AI and former permanent secretary of Kenya's Ministry of Information and Communications
a535.speech: "In Kenya, we saw the number of Internet users more than double in a single year following the liberalisation of markets. We must now bring about the same revolution in broadband costs and access, not only in my country but throughout the world. To achieve that, we are going to bring together our voices, our leadership and our skills to push for competitive and socially responsible markets."

a535.speaker: Jennifer Haroon, principal spokesperson for Google
a535.name: Jennifer Haroon
a535.title: principal spokesperson for Google
a535.speech: "Nearly two out of three people do not have access to the Internet. This is a very large challenge that will not be solved by a single solution or a single actor. The world needs technical innovations and a vision that will allow more people to access the Internet, but we also need a solid strategic foundation favourable to new ideas. By working in collaboration with the Alliance's partners, we can help prepare the ground that will allow us to stimulate innovation and enable more people to benefit from the power of the Internet."

a535.speaker: Ory Okolloh, director of investments at Omidyar Network
a535.name: Ory Okolloh
a535.title: director of investments at Omidyar Network
a535.speech: "The lack of access to affordable Internet in emerging markets is a major obstacle to innovation at scale, which in turn hinders social and economic progress. Omidyar Network is delighted to help lead the creation of the Alliance for Affordable Internet in order to remedy this problem. The Alliance can help millions of people in developing countries gain access to the Internet and open up opportunities for access to information and services, which can significantly improve their lives."

a535.speaker: Dr Rajiv Shah, Administrator of USAID
a535.name: Dr Rajiv Shah
a535.title: Administrator of USAID
a535.speech: "The growing digital divide is a global problem that we must confront together, and we are delighted to be able to work with the committed and diverse group of the Alliance for Affordable Internet, which should allow the most isolated and disadvantaged communities to access the wealth of knowledge and connections that exist within the digital world."

a535.speaker: Professor Tim Unwin, Secretary-General of the Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation
a535.name: Professor Tim Unwin
a535.title: Secretary-General of the Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation
a535.speech: "In a world where information sharing and communications are increasingly driven by the Internet, it is crucial that everyone can access it at affordable prices. The rapid expansion of all types of ICT is, however, bringing about ever greater inequalities in the world, which is why the creation of the Alliance for Affordable Internet is important and comes at a crucial moment. By working together within a carefully constructed partnership, we can try to rebalance these inequalities and turn rhetoric into reality."

a746.speaker: Head of State Protocol of Benin
a746.name: Head of State Protocol of Benin
a746.speech: Instead of inviting the Prime Minister of Guinea, called out the name of Alassane Ouattara; and, instead of saying "allocution" (address), pronounced "allocation" before correcting himself amid murmurs of disapproval from the room.

a746.speaker: Member of the State Protocol (unnamed)
a746.name: Member of the State Protocol (unnamed)
a746.speech: Turned away the US ambassador's representative from the diplomatic corps seating, telling him: "As the ambassador's representative, you have no place here."

a746.speaker: Kevin Amstrong, USAID director, representing the US Ambassador
a746.name: Kevin Amstrong
a746.title: USAID director, representing the US Ambassador
a746.speech: Refused to return to his seat among the ambassadors, and in his approximate French told his interlocutor that he had never seen anything like it.

a753.speaker: Associated Press (report)
a753.name: Associated Press (report)
a753.speech: Reported this week that vast quantities of food aid bearing stamps from the World Food Programme, the US government aid agency USAid, the Japanese government and the Kuwaiti government are for sale in Mogadishu markets; according to the report eight different sites were found to be selling thousands of sacks of food in bulk, and other food aid was also for sale in numerous smaller stores.

a753.speaker: United Nations' World Food Programme
a753.name: United Nations' World Food Programme
a753.speech: In response has rubbished the story, insisting the scale suggested by the AP report was simply implausible; the UN does admit that a certain amount of food aid is indeed being stolen.

a753.speaker: WFP spokesperson in Rome
a753.name: WFP spokesperson in Rome
a753.speech: Told reporters that stolen food sold in Mogadishu markets amounts to no more than "1% of total assistance."

a753.speaker: Somali government (the vestiges of)
a753.name: Somali government (the vestiges of)
a753.speech: Last week called for the creation of a new military force to protect food aid convoys and camps in southern Somalia.

a753.speaker: Reuters (report)
a753.name: Reuters (report)
a753.speech: Reported on Tuesday that Al-Shabaab and Somali government troops as well as African Union peacekeepers were engaged in fierce fighting in northern Mogadishu, prompting doctors and children to flee a hospital that was hit by stray bullets.

a771.speaker: Afar Health Bureau
a771.name: Afar Health Bureau
a771.speech: Says the region has been seeing success in their attempts to convince more people to use the nets.

a771.speaker: Survey (cited)
a771.name: Survey (cited)
a771.speech: A survey indicated that prevention practices were on the rise and that ownership of long lasting insecticide-treated mosquito nets had more than doubled in the last five years.

a771.speaker: Yasin Habib, deputy head of the Afar region’s health bureau
a771.name: Yasin Habib
a771.title: deputy head of the Afar region’s health bureau
a771.speech: “In the past, many died from this disease but now because we can provide better treatment in hospitals, distribute more drugs in the pharmacy and provide nets from donors we have made progress in fighting the disease but we still have a long way to go; just providing nets won’t solve the problem, we need insecticide treated nets, malaria control services, and to continue to raise awareness about prevention,” he said.

a771.speaker: Ethiopian Ministry of Health
a771.name: Ethiopian Ministry of Health
a771.speech: According to the Ministry of Health, about 60 percent of the Ethiopian population lives in Malaria-prone areas and nearly two million cases of malaria were treated last year alone.

a789.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a789.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a789.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a789.speech: Held a consultative meeting with women working across various federal government institutions, focused on empowering Somali women to enhance their roles in promoting security, advancing development, and contributing to nation-building efforts.

a789.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a789.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a789.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a789.speech: Praised the Puntland Darawish forces, acknowledging their extensive operations against ISIS-affiliated Daesh militants in the Bari region, and emphasized the Federal Government's commitment to providing full support to Puntland in ensuring the complete eradication of militant threats and strengthening the nation's security.

a792.speaker: Hassan Dabaleh, prefect of the Tadjourah region
a792.name: Hassan Dabaleh
a792.title: prefect of the Tadjourah region
a792.speech: Delivered the welcome address opening the national dialogue on forced displacement.

a792.speaker: Sirag Omar Abdoulkader, Secretary General of the Ministry of the Interior of Djibouti
a792.name: Sirag Omar Abdoulkader
a792.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of the Interior of Djibouti
a792.speech: Launched the proceedings of the national dialogue, recalling that this is the second meeting on the theme of forced displacement, coming less than a year before the Global Refugee Forum planned for December 2023 ; Indicated that this dialogue should make it possible to identify the drivers and implications of forced displacement and of the protection and assistance offered to refugees in Djibouti, and welcomed the broad participation of the prefectural authorities and of all the stakeholders from the ministerial departments concerned, the regional administrations, the community sector, non-governmental organisations, the private sector and civil society.

a792.speaker: Houssein Hassan Darar, Executive Secretary of ONARS
a792.name: Houssein Hassan Darar
a792.title: Executive Secretary of ONARS
a792.speech: Stressed that Djibouti is a crossroads of human movements, at the heart of a junction linking the African, Asian and European continents, making it a place of transit and a destination for tens of thousands of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants ; "Djibouti is an epicentre of forced displacement in the region, with nearly 35,000 refugees and asylum seekers who are cared for by the Government through ONARS" ; the dialogue is conducive to "a broad reflection on common solutions to forced displacement in Djibouti and thus to promoting the protection of refugees and asylum seekers within the framework of a wider migratory movement."

a792.speaker: Fathia Alwan Aboubaker, Director of the health and social development division of IGAD
a792.name: Fathia Alwan Aboubaker
a792.title: Director of the health and social development division of IGAD
a792.speech: "Our region hosts around 4.5 million refugees and 12 million displaced persons" ; said IGAD is mobilised close to "the many displaced populations" who "have difficulty breaking free from the cycle of dependence on humanitarian aid and finding durable solutions" ; "Djibouti is a direct beneficiary of the Development Response to Displacement Impacts Project (DRDIP), which has transformed refugee-hosting areas through community initiatives. Djibouti is also working with IGAD's regional Migration Fund on health" ; concluded by underlining that the national dialogue will bring together the various stakeholders working on forced displacement in the country to improve the coherence of responses and strengthen collaboration between ministries, technical departments, agencies and stakeholders.

a799.speaker: Muslim World League
a799.name: Muslim World League
a799.speech: Condemned in the strongest terms the continued violations of all international laws and norms by the Israeli occupation government, including its announcement regarding the incursion into and control of the Gaza Strip and the Palestinian territories.

a799.speaker: Sheikh Dr. Muhammad bin Abdul Karim Al-Issa, Secretary General of the Muslim World League and Chairman of the Association of Muslim Scholars (statement issued by the League's General Secretariat)
a799.name: Sheikh Dr. Muhammad bin Abdul Karim Al-Issa
a799.title: Secretary General of the Muslim World League and Chairman of the Association of Muslim Scholars (statement issued by the League's General Secretariat)
a799.speech: Condemned this barbaric approach of the Israeli occupation government, categorically rejecting all of its expansionist attempts, which violate resolutions of international legitimacy and undermine efforts to achieve a just and comprehensive peace in the region.

a873.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USaid) (stop-work order and award suspension notice)
a873.name: United States Agency for International Development (USaid) (stop-work order and award suspension notice)
a873.speech: Has issued a stop-work order (SWO) and award suspension notice to its implementing partners in Malawi; the notice, dated January 27 2025, requires implementing partners to cease activities under existing agreements and halt any expenditures related to ongoing projects; affected organisations have been instructed to notify their sub-awardees about the suspension and take measures to minimise costs already incurred ; has pledged to provide further guidance soon.

a873.speaker: Executive order ‘Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid’
a873.name: Executive order ‘Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid’
a873.speech: Mandates a comprehensive review of US foreign assistance programmes to ensure alignment with American interests.

a873.speaker: Executive order ‘Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programmes and Preferencing’
a873.name: Executive order ‘Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programmes and Preferencing’
a873.speech: Specifically targets diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility (DEIA)-related activities.

a873.speaker: Natalie Thunberg, USaid Supervisory Contracting and Agreement Officer
a873.name: Natalie Thunberg
a873.title: USaid Supervisory Contracting and Agreement Officer
a873.speech: According to her, partners must confirm the cessation of DEIA-related activities or certify that their projects do not involve DEIA elements ; “Your organisation must immediately comply with this notice.”

a873.speaker: US Embassy in Malawi
a873.name: US Embassy in Malawi
a873.speech: Responded to inquiries, stating “the suspension aligns with broader policy shifts intended to reassess the strategic value and effectiveness of US foreign aid investments”; further assured that USaid was committed to a smooth transition and that it had provided resources for partners to seek clarifications; according to the embassy, partners are encouraged to submit questions via a designated form and sign up for updates through USaid’s implementing partner portal.

a873.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Malawi Information Minister
a873.name: Moses Kunkuyu
a873.title: Malawi Information Minister
a873.speech: Said developed countries such as the US knew and appreciated that Malawi was one country that had invested heavily in efforts to eradicate poverty, disease and other socio-economic ills ; said, being a repetitive victim of natural disasters and global economic woes, it was clear that Malawi still needed a hand from development partners “while we enhance our economic recovery endeavors” ; said the recent resumption of direct budgetary support from some donors was an indication that helping Malawi through various programmes was not helping a consuming Malawi but, rather, helping Malawi to stand on its feet ; “It is, therefore, in the interest of Malawi for rich countries to continue developing suitable partnering arrangements with countries like Malawi as reliable partners in the global development agenda.”

a880.speaker: City of Windhoek council
a880.name: City of Windhoek council
a880.speech: noted that “If the budget allocation is not utilised due to challenges and difficulties on the ground, it is reduced during the city’s budget review period in September-October; a mismatch between the city and national government’s financial years.”

a880.speaker: Financial model prepared under the collaboration agreement between the municipal council and the USAID Southern Africa Energy Programme (SAEP)
a880.name: Financial model prepared under the collaboration agreement between the municipal council and the USAID Southern Africa Energy Programme (SAEP)
a880.speech: shows the city will require over N$700 million over eight years to complete the electrification of Windhoek’s informal settlement areas.

a880.speaker: City of Windhoek (statement released by the city)
a880.name: City of Windhoek (statement released by the city)
a880.speech: “This means that the City of Windhoek needs N$100 million annually over the next eight years. In light of this, the city’s strategic executives for electricity and finance were granted approval to approach financial institutions on behalf of the City of Windhoek for the financing of the electrification in Windhoek’s informal settlements.”

a880.speaker: National Emergency Care Centre (NECC) application dated 5 July 2021
a880.name: National Emergency Care Centre (NECC) application dated 5 July 2021
a880.speech: indicated that the applicant will set up a Section 21 entity, and will be filling the gap between public and private healthcare facilities in the quality and cost of services.

a880.speaker: Council documents (conditions of approval)
a880.name: Council documents (conditions of approval)
a880.speech: “The applicant must implement an appropriate healthcare risk waste management system to ensure that all the waste generated at the facility is properly disposed of. The applicant will be responsible for running expenses, including water, electricity and security services. The applicant will not pay rent, as this will be offset as council’s contribution towards the noble project.”

a1152.speaker: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a1152.name: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS)
a1152.speech: Warned that recent decisions by the United States to suspend funding to Ethiopia's national HIV response will be "particularly severe", affecting more than 270,000 beneficiaries across the country's Oromia and Gambella regions, as well as Addis Ababa ; In a statement released on Thursday said the "pause of U.S. assistance to community programs and drop-in centers serving women, young girls, and priority populations at higher risk of HIV infection means tens of thousands of individuals will no longer be able to access critical services." ; The agency further noted that "the closure of many drop-in centers and the termination of outreach workers' and peer educators' contracts will effectively shut off support to vulnerable groups."

a1152.speaker: Ethiopia's Ministry of Health (MoH)
a1152.name: Ethiopia's Ministry of Health (MoH)
a1152.speech: On Wednesday instructed health bureaux to halt all activities and payments related to employees hired under the U.S. government budget support, citing the termination of funding from the USAID.

a1152.speaker: USAID
a1152.name: USAID
a1152.speech: Said the disruption of service in Addis Ababa, Oromia, and Gambella will put 235,560 people at risk of new HIV infections and sexually transmitted diseases.

a1171.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice President, and Heiko Josef Maas, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Germany (joint op-ed)
a1171.name: Josep Borrell
a1171.title: EU High Representative/Vice President, and Heiko Josef Maas, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Germany (joint op-ed)
a1171.speech: Write that they offered the new Sudanese authorities their full support; that keeping the drive towards reform is vital and should soon lead to the establishment of the transitional legislative council and the appointment of civilian state governors, and that the dividends of the transition must reach the whole of Sudan, including states marked by year-long conflicts, such as Darfur, Blue Nile and South Kordofan. They warn that the COVID-19 pandemic puts the achievements of Sudan's peaceful revolution in jeopardy and argue that "to provide a lifeline to the on-going transition and accompany Sudan's own efforts, increased international political and financial assistance remains essential. The moment to do so is now to avoid any backsliding in the transition." They state that on 25 June the United Nations, the European Union, Germany and Sudan will convene an international conference to send a strong message to the Sudanese people: "the international community continues to stand behind your democratic transition!", that around 50 countries and international organisations are offering Sudan a partnership to support the country up to the elections in 2022, that they plan to raise enough funds to kick-start a social protection programme by the World Bank and the Sudanese Government and will also support the International Monetary Fund in opening up Sudan's road towards debt relief. They conclude: "A democratic Sudan remains the best guarantee for the long-term stability of the country and the entire region... our message to them must be: your sacrifices were not in vain. The 'new Sudan' is here to stay. We won't let you fall."

a1171.speaker: Sudan's first civilian Government in over 30 years
a1171.name: Sudan's first civilian Government in over 30 years
a1171.speech: Pledged to meet the peoples' aspirations for "freedom, peace and justice".

a1171.speaker: UN Security Council
a1171.name: UN Security Council
a1171.speech: A few weeks ago it agreed to mandate a new political UN mission to assist Sudan on its road to peace and democracy.

a1171.speaker: Sudanese protesters (chant)
a1171.name: Sudanese protesters (chant)
a1171.speech: "Just fall, that's all" was one of the slogans that protesters chanted on the streets of Khartoum to oust the old regime.

a1463.speaker: US Department of Justice (emergency filing to the Supreme Court)
a1463.name: US Department of Justice (emergency filing to the Supreme Court)
a1463.speech: Asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday to intervene in the administration's efforts to withhold billions of dollars from foreign aid organizations and lift an injunction that is forcing it to keep making payments; noted in the emergency filing that a 2-1 panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit earlier this month ruled the injunction should be overturned.

a1463.speaker: Trump administration (Supreme Court filing)
a1463.name: Trump administration (Supreme Court filing)
a1463.speech: Said the congressionally appropriated funds subject to the injunction comprise tens of billions of dollars, some $12 billion of which would need to be spent by the U.S. Department of State before September 30, when they expire; said that without the justices' intervention, it will be forced to keep making payments before the expiration date, "overriding the Executive Branch's foreign-policy judgments regarding whether to pursue rescissions and thwarting interbranch dialogue."

a1463.speaker: AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition and Journalism Development Network (litigation)
a1463.name: AIDS Vaccine Advocacy Coalition and Journalism Development Network (litigation)
a1463.speech: Brought litigation alleging Trump's funding freeze was unlawful.

a1463.speaker: Lawyers for the plaintiffs
a1463.name: Lawyers for the plaintiffs
a1463.speech: Did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

a1463.speaker: Amir Ali, US District Judge (Washington-based)
a1463.name: Amir Ali
a1463.title: US District Judge (Washington-based)
a1463.speech: Ordered the Trump administration to pay nearly $2 billion in outstanding aid to its humanitarian partners worldwide; rejected on Monday a request to put his injunction on hold.

a1463.speaker: Karen Henderson, US Circuit Judge, writing for the D.C. Circuit panel majority
a1463.name: Karen Henderson
a1463.title: US Circuit Judge, writing for the D.C. Circuit panel majority
a1463.speech: Ruled that the nonprofit groups failed to satisfy the requirements for an injunction, saying only the U.S. Government Accountability Office, a watchdog agency, could challenge Trump's efforts to withhold the funding.

a1469.speaker: Dorothée Kindé Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
a1469.name: Dorothée Kindé Gazard
a1469.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a1469.speech: reiterated during the meeting with the technical and financial partners (PTF) the government's commitment to carry out major actions with these resources. According to her, this signing marks the materialisation of the Beninese government's commitment to work for the improvement of the health of the population ; stressed that, managed on the basis of the results-based financing approach, this compact will make it possible to coordinate effectively the actions of the PTFs at departmental and national level ; "The year 2015 is a year of great challenges and of consolidating the gains," she assured.

a1469.speaker: Dorothée Kindé Gazard, Minister of Health of Benin
a1469.name: Dorothée Kindé Gazard
a1469.title: Minister of Health of Benin
a1469.speech: emphasised, regarding the record of actions in the health sector: "All of which improved the rate of coverage of staffing needs from 66.06% in 2013 to 74.05% in 2014" ; according to her, the contingency plan against the Ebola and Lassa haemorrhagic fever epidemics worked perfectly and the conclusions are reassuring.

a1469.speaker: Kevin Armstrong, Director of USAID, lead of the technical and financial partners (PTF)
a1469.name: Kevin Armstrong
a1469.title: Director of USAID, lead of the technical and financial partners (PTF)
a1469.speech: said Benin has recorded a great deal of progress in the health sector. "We stand by your side to achieve the results," he said on behalf of the international and non-governmental organisations that are parties to the agreement ; the spokesman of the health sector PTFs said he was convinced that the approach would serve to improve the MDG indicators.

a1469.speaker: The Beninese side (government)
a1469.name: The Beninese side (government)
a1469.speech: also welcomed the fact that the signing of this compact will allow a consensual process of monitoring the tools, approaches, mechanisms and indicators for tracking the integrated annual work plan.

a1543.speaker: Cina Lawson, Minister of Digital Economy & Digital Transformation of Togo, and Rory Stewart, former foreign aid minister of the United Kingdom and senior adviser at GiveDirectly (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1543.name: Cina Lawson
a1543.title: Minister of Digital Economy & Digital Transformation of Togo, and Rory Stewart, former foreign aid minister of the United Kingdom and senior adviser at GiveDirectly (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1543.speech: Argued that with 700 million people living on less than 2.15 dollars a day, the need for scalable solutions has never been more urgent, and that direct cash transfers to the poorest households are a solution that can be scaled up rapidly to accelerate the end of extreme poverty. They note that less than five percent of the 200 billion dollars spent annually on international development is allocated to cash transfers, while new digital technologies have dramatically lowered the cost of delivering money safely to the poorest parts of the world.

a1543.speaker: Cina Lawson, Minister of Digital Economy & Digital Transformation of Togo, and Rory Stewart, former foreign aid minister of the United Kingdom and senior adviser at GiveDirectly (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1543.name: Cina Lawson
a1543.title: Minister of Digital Economy & Digital Transformation of Togo, and Rory Stewart, former foreign aid minister of the United Kingdom and senior adviser at GiveDirectly (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a1543.speech: Building on the insights of an international working group they recently co-chaired, propose establishing a new global fund to eradicate extreme poverty through lump-sum direct cash transfers, funded by a mix of philanthropists, institutions and governments, similar to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, and offered as a complement rather than a substitute for other interventions: "For the first time, the world has the money and the methods to succeed. What are we waiting for?"

a1543.speaker: More than 300 randomised control trials (cited research)
a1543.name: More than 300 randomised control trials (cited research)
a1543.speech: The upshot is that transfers can boost incomes more than twofold; increase school enrollment and entrepreneurship; decrease skipped meals, illness, and depression; and reduce domestic violence. They neither reduce hours worked nor increase spending on tempting goods like tobacco and alcohol, and every one dollar transfer has a spillover effect of around 2.50 dollars in the local economy.

a1543.speaker: Recent research from Kenya (cited study)
a1543.name: Recent research from Kenya (cited study)
a1543.speech: Showed that a 500-dollar lump-sum cash transfer was particularly effective in empowering families to make income-generating investments.

a1608.speaker: Peter Kapala, Zambian Minister of Energy
a1608.name: Peter Kapala
a1608.title: Zambian Minister of Energy
a1608.speech: Speaking at the official opening of Surya Bio Energy Limited filling station in Lusaka, said access to affordable energy was vital to the economic and social development of the country ; said government was doing everything possible to ensure that Zambians were given access to clean and affordable energy ; said the blending of 20 percent ethanol and 80 percent of unleaded petrol had proved to work well in vehicles without causing any damages ; disclosed that the programme would first run for six months as it was being monitored by government, the Ethanol Production of Zambia and Surya Bio Energy Limited.

a1608.speaker: Kamesh Patel, Chairperson of Surya Bio Energy Limited
a1608.name: Kamesh Patel
a1608.title: Chairperson of Surya Bio Energy Limited
a1608.speech: Said Zambia would no longer need to import fuel as the country could rise to a fuel-producing country using ethanol ; said ethanol was environment friendly as it had no emissions and that Surya company would depend on Zambian cassava farmers for the market to produce ethanol ; commended the government for supporting the project and for allowing Surya Energy Limited to work on the ethanol plant.

a1608.speaker: Linnisa Wahid, U.S. Embassy Zambia Chargé d'Affaires
a1608.name: Linnisa Wahid
a1608.title: U.S. Embassy Zambia Chargé d'Affaires
a1608.speech: Said, when officially swearing in the 20 new Peace Corps Volunteers, that since the Peace Corps volunteers arrived in Zambia in 1994, more than 2,500 Volunteers have lived and worked in rural communities throughout the country.

a1872.speaker: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
a1872.name: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
a1872.speech: has secured the conviction of human trafficker, Fasa Sandra, over trafficking of persons for prostitution; had arraigned Fasa Sandra, 35, and Omengor Chinoso, 26, before a Federal High Court for exportation of persons for prostitution and tampering with evidence and witness in 2021.

a1872.speaker: Federal High Court (court record)
a1872.name: Federal High Court (court record)
a1872.speech: Sandra was sentenced to two years jail term with an option of N250,000 fine; the court reserved judgment on Omengor Chinoso, who had jumped bail, pending when she was brought back to the court.

a1913.speaker: Treasury of Zimbabwe
a1913.name: Treasury of Zimbabwe
a1913.speech: Has said manufacturing sector output will grow by 2,4 percent this year, 0,7 percentage points weaker than earlier projections of 3,1 percent on account of anticipated production challenges in the cement sector (presenting the 2025 Mid-Term Budget).

a1933.speaker: White House (first draft of the budget for Donald Trump's second term)
a1933.name: White House (first draft of the budget for Donald Trump's second term)
a1933.speech: On 2 May 2025 presented the first draft of the budget for Donald Trump's second term, a document that drastically reduces funding allocated to non-military programmes, sparing only military and security spending.

a1933.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1933.name: Donald Trump
a1933.title: US President
a1933.speech: Following the announcement, planned a 22% reduction in non-military public spending, equivalent to 163 billion dollars.

a1933.speaker: Francois Giovalucci, researcher and former officer of the French Development Agency (AFD), and Thierry Vircoulon, researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (Ifri)
a1933.name: Francois Giovalucci
a1933.title: researcher and former officer of the French Development Agency (AFD), and Thierry Vircoulon, researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (Ifri)
a1933.speech: Said this shift in the aid paradigm is happening not only in Washington but also in Europe. They stress that budgets earmarked for international aid are shrinking everywhere, even under Labour governments such as in the United Kingdom, where it even led to the resignation of the minister responsible for the file.

a1933.speaker: Francois Giovalucci, researcher and former officer of the French Development Agency (AFD), and Thierry Vircoulon, researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (Ifri)
a1933.name: Francois Giovalucci
a1933.title: researcher and former officer of the French Development Agency (AFD), and Thierry Vircoulon, researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (Ifri)
a1933.speech: Note that a new approach to aid seems to be emerging, favouring less public and increasingly privatised interventions, with support directed more and more towards the private sector and collaboration with private actors, which amounts to a form of double privatisation of what was once considered official development assistance.

a1933.speaker: White House
a1933.name: White House
a1933.speech: Announced the ending of family planning programmes in Africa.

a2018.speaker: IMF Regional Economic Outlook for sub-Saharan Africa (analytical note)
a2018.name: IMF Regional Economic Outlook for sub-Saharan Africa (analytical note)
a2018.speech: “Our analytical note for the latest Regional Economic Outlook for sub-Saharan Africa takes a closer look at this issue” — finding that over the past ten years growth in sub-Saharan Africa’s resource-intensive countries (RICs), especially fuel exporters such as Angola, Chad and Nigeria, has slowed sharply, falling far below growth in non-RICs such as Ethiopia, Rwanda and Senegal, with incomes in RICs essentially stagnating.

a2018.speaker: IMF staff analysis
a2018.name: IMF staff analysis
a2018.speech: Confirms that terms-of-trade shocks have a stronger and longer-lasting impact on growth in countries with weak governance ; “We estimate that for every one-percent worsening in a country’s terms of trade, medium-term growth is around ¼ percentage point higher in countries with smaller governance challenges.”

a2034.speaker: Fraser Institute
a2034.name: Fraser Institute
a2034.speech: Said it contributed to Namibia's score in its annual Policy Perception Index for 2023 decreasing 20 points from 87.22 in 2019 to 68, dropping Namibia from position 14 out of 76 jurisdictions, down to 33 out of 86.

a2034.speaker: Isabella Chirchir, mining commissioner, and Erasmus Shivolo, deputy mining commissioner
a2034.name: Isabella Chirchir
a2034.title: mining commissioner, and Erasmus Shivolo, deputy mining commissioner
a2034.speech: According to them, the suggestion is still in development, and discussions with the ministry of finance are ongoing.

a2034.speaker: Erasmus Shivolo, deputy mining commissioner
a2034.name: Erasmus Shivolo
a2034.title: deputy mining commissioner
a2034.speech: Made reference to Epangelo, the government's mining enterprise, which enjoys preference for strategic mineral licences and holds 10% of the massive Husab uranium mine, and 7.5% of Navachab gold mine, among others.

a2034.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.name: Veston Malango
a2034.title: Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.speech: Said the policy proposal is on the table, and the chamber has been engaging the minister and the mining ministry since it was introduced. Further clarity is needed, he said, adding that the chamber is working on models to present to government, which will detail the consequences of a free carry policy for mines. "We have highlighted that free carry is an additional cost. The final decision should be informed by well-researched models. The objective is obviously more benefits from the mineral resource coming to government. The question comes in: Will you have more with that scenario than what you are getting right now?"

a2034.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.name: Veston Malango
a2034.title: Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.speech: Recently told parliament that in the last five years, the industry paid close to N$9.7 billion in royalties to government, export levies worth N$1.32 billion, dividends of N$3.4 billion and corporate tax of N$11.44 billion, all amounting to N$25.84 billion in government income.

a2034.speaker: Veston Malango, Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.name: Veston Malango
a2034.title: Chamber of Mines of Namibia CEO
a2034.speech: "Our minister has proposed to us, and we have accepted, that these discussions must firstly be at a technical level, between the executive director of the ministry of finance, the executive director of ministry of mines and ourselves, and that is where we are," he said. ; "Hats off to our government that they don't just come and decree, but it is a proposal that has been put on the table, and now it is subject for engagement," he said.

a2138.speaker: Mzuzu University (Mzuni) Department of AgriSciences, paper titled 'Assessing the military upholding of the Constitution in democracy to promote national food security in Malawi' (co-authored by former MDF Commander General Vincent Nundwe (retired), former Moyale Barracks commanding officer Thoko Chazema, army officials Mavuto Tembo, Hope Ngilazi, David Kumwenda and historian Chrispin Mphande)
a2138.name: Mzuzu University (Mzuni) Department of AgriSciences
a2138.title: paper titled 'Assessing the military upholding of the Constitution in democracy to promote national food security in Malawi' (co-authored by former MDF Commander General Vincent Nundwe (retired), former Moyale Barracks commanding officer Thoko Chazema, army officials Mavuto Tembo, Hope Ngilazi, David Kumwenda and historian Chrispin Mphande)
a2138.speech: Highlighted corruption by some public officers and unlawful influence as some factors frustrating Malawi Defence Force (MDF) efforts to ensure food security in the country; noted that allowing increased military involvement in non-traditional missions erodes the authority of institutions mandated with internal security; and noted that in January 2023, MDF and police intercepted 25 truckloads of maize carrying 575 metric tonnes heading for Tanzania amid an export ban. ; "The challenge is that some of the concerned departments flouted procedures such as giving fake documentations because of professional mediocrity because of corruption. Politicians wanted to intervene without lawful authority to direct planning of such [maize export] activities." ; The authors further observe that some junior military officials get carried away in non-traditional missions and get entangled in corrupt behaviours.

a2138.speaker: Mark Katsonga Phiri, then minister of Trade and Industry (Malawi)
a2138.name: Mark Katsonga Phiri
a2138.title: then minister of Trade and Industry (Malawi)
a2138.speech: Said owners of impounded trucks and maize were allegedly connected to politicians.

a2160.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.name: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta
a2160.title: Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.speech: Calls for bold political commitment and increased domestic resource allocation to support the country's HIV response amid global donor funding challenges: "The fight against the spread of HIV remains a national priority that requires our collective efforts, partnership, and collaboration; we call for a united front to address structural barriers such as stigma and discrimination that impede access to HIV testing and treatment services." She notes that inadequate domestic resource allocation for HIV response in Liberia continues to undermine efforts to sustain gains beyond 2030, stressing that it is time now to own and sustain these achievements as a country. She explains that this year's World AIDS Day is globally themed, "Collective Action, and Sustain and Accelerate HIV progress," which aligns with Liberia's commitment to ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

a2160.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.name: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta
a2160.title: Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.speech: Announced that with support from UNAID, NAC has initiated the development of a National HIV Sustainability Roadmap to transform Liberia's HIV response into a more self-reliant system, and that the roadmap will prioritize increased domestic financing, as outlined in the updated National HIV and AIDS Strategic Plan (2021-2026).

a2160.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.name: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta
a2160.title: Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.speech: Acknowledges partners' contributions, including PEPFAR, the Global Fund, UN agencies, and civil society organizations, for their unwavering support in combating HIV in Liberia: "We also recognize the efforts of civil society organizations that continue to stand up for the voiceless and the donor community for their commitment to the national HIV response."

a2160.speaker: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta, Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.name: Dr. Cecelia J. Nuta
a2160.title: Chairperson of the National Aids Commission of Liberia
a2160.speech: Appeals to policymakers, private sector actors, and community leaders to play active roles in sustaining gains made over the years ; "Community outreach will engage opinion leaders to reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination while creating demand for HIV testing" ; urges Liberians to rally behind the national theme: "We want to humbly appeal to all state actors, policymakers, and the private sector to get involved."

a2227.speaker: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2227.name: Board of Directors of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2227.speech: Decided, at its quarterly ordinary session on Wednesday 10 January 2014, that Benin is henceforth eligible for the second compact of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA), after having been rejected in December 2013 for failing to validate the "control of corruption" indicator.

a2227.speaker: Samuel Batcho, MCA-Benin coordinator
a2227.name: Samuel Batcho
a2227.title: MCA-Benin coordinator
a2227.speech: Said to national television (ORTB) yesterday evening: "Benin will no longer be in a limited engagement with the MCC. It can move forward with the signing of the second compact," and added that the second compact would probably be signed in the first quarter of 2015 at the latest.

a2244.speaker: United Nations (80th session General Assembly theme document)
a2244.name: United Nations (80th session General Assembly theme document)
a2244.speech: The theme proposed for the general debate of the 80th session is: "Better together: more than 80 years in the service of peace, development and human rights."

a2244.speaker: Israel
a2244.name: Israel
a2244.speech: Repeatedly attacked the UN, for example for criticising its conduct of the war in Gaza; the organisation was accused of antisemitism and Secretary-General António Guterres was declared persona non grata.

a2244.speaker: United Nations
a2244.name: United Nations
a2244.speech: Made increasingly desperate appeals to end the massacre of innocents in Gaza and Sudan and to allow emergency humanitarian aid to reach the most vulnerable.

a2333.speaker: Senior Gen. Min Aung Hlaing, head of Myanmar's military government
a2333.name: Senior Gen. Min Aung Hlaing
a2333.title: head of Myanmar's military government
a2333.speech: "The death toll and injuries are expected to rise," he said as he announced on television that at least 144 people were killed and 730 others were injured in his country; said Myanmar was ready to accept foreign assistance.

a2333.speaker: Authorities in Bangkok, Thailand
a2333.name: Authorities in Bangkok
a2333.title: Thailand
a2333.speech: Said six people were killed, 22 were injured and 101 were missing from three construction sites, including the high-rise; revised the death toll Saturday morning from 10 reported the previous day, saying several critically injured people were mistakenly reported dead.

a2333.speaker: Chadchart Sittipunt, Bangkok Governor
a2333.name: Chadchart Sittipunt
a2333.title: Bangkok Governor
a2333.speech: Said that more people were believed to be alive in the wreckage as search efforts continued Saturday morning.

a2333.speaker: U.S. Geological Survey
a2333.name: U.S. Geological Survey
a2333.speech: Estimated that the death toll could top 1,000; the USGS and Germany's GFZ centre for geosciences said the earthquake was a shallow 10 kilometres (6.2 miles), according to preliminary reports.

a2333.speaker: Myanmar's government
a2333.name: Myanmar's government
a2333.speech: Said blood was in high demand in the hardest-hit areas.

a2333.speaker: Xinhua news agency (official)
a2333.name: Xinhua news agency (official)
a2333.speech: Reported that a 37-member team from the Chinese province of Yunnan reached the city of Yangon early Saturday with earthquake detectors, drones and other supplies.

a2333.speaker: Tass, Russian state news agency
a2333.name: Tass
a2333.title: Russian state news agency
a2333.speech: Reported that Russia's emergencies ministry dispatched two planes carrying 120 rescuers and supplies.

a2333.speaker: India's foreign minister (post on X)
a2333.name: India's foreign minister (post on X)
a2333.speech: Posted that India sent a search and rescue team and a medical team as well as blankets, tarpaulin, hygiene kits, sleeping bags, solar lamps, food packets and kitchen sets.

a2333.speaker: Malaysia's foreign ministry
a2333.name: Malaysia's foreign ministry
a2333.speech: Said the country will send 50 people on Sunday to help identify and provide aid to the worst-hit areas.

a2333.speaker: President Donald Trump
a2333.name: President Donald Trump
a2333.speech: Said Friday that the U.S. was going to help with the response.

a2333.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a2333.name: Experts (unnamed)
a2333.speech: Were concerned about the U.S. relief effort given the Trump administration's deep cuts in foreign assistance.

a2333.speaker: Mohammed Riyas, the International Rescue Committee's Myanmar director
a2333.name: Mohammed Riyas
a2333.title: the International Rescue Committee's Myanmar director
a2333.speech: "We fear it may be weeks before we understand the full extent of destruction caused by this earthquake."

a2333.speaker: Global New Light of Myanmar, Myanmar's English-language state newspaper
a2333.name: Global New Light of Myanmar
a2333.title: Myanmar's English-language state newspaper
a2333.speech: Said five cities and towns had seen building collapses and two bridges had fallen, including one on a key highway between Mandalay and Yangon.

a2333.speaker: Christian Aid
a2333.name: Christian Aid
a2333.speech: Said its partners and colleagues on the ground reported that a dam burst in the city, causing water levels to rise in the lowland areas.

a2333.speaker: Julie Mehigan, who oversees Christian Aid's work in Asia, the Middle East and Europe
a2333.name: Julie Mehigan
a2333.title: who oversees Christian Aid's work in Asia, the Middle East and Europe
a2333.speech: "this disaster will have left people devastated"; "Even before this heartbreaking earthquake, we know conflict and displacement has left countless people in real need."

a2333.speaker: United Nations
a2333.name: United Nations
a2333.speech: Says more than 3 million people have been displaced by the fighting in Myanmar and nearly 20 million are in need.

a2333.speaker: Suriya Juangroongruangkit, Thai Deputy Prime Minister
a2333.name: Suriya Juangroongruangkit
a2333.title: Thai Deputy Prime Minister
a2333.speech: "It's a great tragedy," he said after viewing the site of the collapsed building.

a2333.speaker: Voranoot Thirawat, a lawyer working in central Bangkok
a2333.name: Voranoot Thirawat
a2333.title: a lawyer working in central Bangkok
a2333.speech: Said she first realised something was wrong when she saw a light swinging back and forth, then heard the building creaking, and she and her colleagues fled down 12 flights of stairs: "In my lifetime, there was no earthquake like this in Bangkok."

a2333.speaker: Fraser Morton, a tourist from Scotland
a2333.name: Fraser Morton
a2333.title: a tourist from Scotland
a2333.speech: "All of a sudden, the whole building began to move. Immediately, there was screaming and a lot of panic," he said, adding that some people fled down upward-moving escalators.

a2333.speaker: Paul Vincent, a tourist visiting from England
a2333.name: Paul Vincent
a2333.title: a tourist visiting from England
a2333.speech: Recalled seeing a high-rise building swaying, water falling from a rooftop pool and people crying in the streets.

a2333.speaker: Chinese media reports
a2333.name: Chinese media reports
a2333.speech: Reported that the earthquake was felt in China's Yunnan and Sichuan provinces and caused damage and injuries in the city of Ruili on the border with Myanmar.

a2333.speaker: A resident of Mangshi, China (unnamed), speaking to The Paper
a2333.name: A resident of Mangshi
a2333.title: China (unnamed), speaking to The Paper
a2333.speech: Said the shaking in Mangshi, a Chinese city about 100 kilometers northeast of Ruili, was so strong that people couldn't stand.

a2671.speaker: White House
a2671.name: White House
a2671.speech: Disclosed the agreement on Friday (that Egypt accepts the passage of humanitarian aid for Gaza).

a2671.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2671.name: United Nations (UN)
a2671.speech: Has already admitted that humanitarian aid, namely food, has been falling drastically since Israel's offensive in Rafah began ; said it could not be at Kerem Shalom collecting the aid, since it has become too dangerous as the fighting has increased ; stated that in the last 19 days 143 trucks made the crossing.

a2671.speaker: International Court of Justice
a2671.name: International Court of Justice
a2671.speech: On Friday ordered Israel to suspend the offensive in Rafah.

a2671.speaker: Israeli authorities
a2671.name: Israeli authorities
a2671.speech: According to them, hundreds of other trucks are stopped in Gaza.

a2671.speaker: Official Israeli figures
a2671.name: Official Israeli figures
a2671.speech: According to official Israeli data, the Hamas attack on Israeli soil of 7 October 2023 caused around 1,200 deaths, mostly civilians.

a2671.speaker: Israeli army (Tel Aviv army)
a2671.name: Israeli army (Tel Aviv army)
a2671.speech: According to it, 121 people currently remain held in Gaza, of whom 37 are already believed to be dead.

a3122.speaker: Colonel Hassane Chaibou, Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.name: Colonel Hassane Chaibou
a3122.title: Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.speech: According to him, the first pickaxe blows for the establishment of Niamey's green belt were struck in 1965; at the time the space had benefited from political commitment, strong involvement of technicians and a responsible citizenship, but unfortunately over time, with the urbanization of Niamey, the initial objectives are far from being achieved given the multiplication of forms of pressure that degrade it day by day and year by year.

a3122.speaker: Colonel Hassane Chaibou, Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.name: Colonel Hassane Chaibou
a3122.title: Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.speech: Said these individuals of course benefited from political connections at a certain moment and from complicities of all kinds. ; According to him the infamy perpetrated against the green belt, a common heritage, is quite simply absurd, and there are several levels of responsibility. ; He explained that there had been 389.15 ha in excess of the areas officially authorized by the Ministry of Urban Planning.

a3122.speaker: Colonel Hassane Chaibou, Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.name: Colonel Hassane Chaibou
a3122.title: Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.speech: Explains that another reason for the choice of the neem rests on the fact that it is a shade species serving as resting places for city dwellers.

a3122.speaker: Colonel Hassane Chaibou, Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.name: Colonel Hassane Chaibou
a3122.title: Regional Director of the Environment, Water Resources and Sanitation of Niamey
a3122.speech: Specifies that the objectives assigned to the recovered space include the creation of an adequate framework for scientific research, the improvement of the populations' living environment and the creation of a natural setting of relaxation and leisure for young people, through five major actions: a botanical garden, a water park, a zoological park, a sports area and a relaxation area suited to all ages. “Our priority is now to clean up the space and secure it while awaiting the implementation of the development works,” he concluded.

a3122.speaker: Law of 8 June 2004 on the forestry regime in Niger and decree of 9 July 2004 on the protection of green spaces and green belts (legal texts)
a3122.name: Law of 8 June 2004 on the forestry regime in Niger and decree of 9 July 2004 on the protection of green spaces and green belts (legal texts)
a3122.speech: State clearly that “any occupation of the green belt that is not the object of a declassification remains and stays illegal.”

a3122.speaker: Decree 2004-200 of 09 January 2004 (legal text)
a3122.name: Decree 2004-200 of 09 January 2004 (legal text)
a3122.speech: Underlines that any act involving land in the green belt must be the subject of a joint authorization from the Ministers of Urban Planning and of the Environment.

a3175.speaker: Gaston Cossi Dossouhoui, Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries of Benin
a3175.name: Gaston Cossi Dossouhoui
a3175.title: Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries of Benin
a3175.speech: Stressed that the campaign he had just launched is not a routine one: "These two diseases, foot-and-mouth disease and lumpy skin disease, have appeared and are wreaking havoc. They are decimating herds. Faced with these problems, ProSeR decided to take charge of making these two vaccines available, with the support of its financial partner, the West African Development Bank (BOAD)." ; Specified that the foot-and-mouth vaccine costs 2,600 CFA francs but is sold to the farmer at 1,400 CFA francs, and the lumpy skin disease vaccine costs only 100 CFA francs ; "These are life-saving actions by the Government to support this vital sector that is livestock farming. It is a godsend for having fat calves and healthy meat."

a3175.speaker: Roukayath Chabi Toko, Coordinator of ProSeR (Ruminant Herd Sedentarization Project)
a3175.name: Roukayath Chabi Toko
a3175.title: Coordinator of ProSeR (Ruminant Herd Sedentarization Project)
a3175.speech: Specified that without the vaccinations, the project's actions would be in vain.

a3175.speaker: Abdoulaye Bombouya, Representative of the livestock farmers
a3175.name: Abdoulaye Bombouya
a3175.title: Representative of the livestock farmers
a3175.speech: "It is an immense joy for us. For all the livestock farmers of Benin, it is a great event. These diseases wreak havoc among our herds. We commit to mobilizing all farmers to have their herds vaccinated. We thank the Government, ProSeR and the BOAD for this support."

a3175.speaker: Sandra Amichia, Resident Representative of the BOAD (West African Development Bank) in Benin
a3175.name: Sandra Amichia
a3175.title: Resident Representative of the BOAD (West African Development Bank) in Benin
a3175.speech: Said the National Association of Professional Organizations of Ruminant Farmers of Benin (ANOPER) has committed to contributing to the success of the campaign, in line with the Institution's objectives ; "The BOAD is determined to accompany the process, alongside the Beninese Government, so that what has begun can be carried through to the end. Our wish is that livestock farmers become self-reliant in the long run. That is the BOAD's will."

a3181.speaker: Hleziphi Nkomo, project coordinator
a3181.name: Hleziphi Nkomo
a3181.title: project coordinator
a3181.speech: Told New Ziana that the district's natural wealth was being harnessed to improve the lives of local communities: "We are exporting seeds to Germany, capitalising on the abundance in our region. So far, we have exported eight tons, and the company is returning soon for more. This is just the beginning, we want to keep growing this market."

a3181.speaker: Hleziphi Nkomo, project coordinator
a3181.name: Hleziphi Nkomo
a3181.title: project coordinator
a3181.speech: Said while marula nuts remain plentiful, ximenia seeds were hit hard by the heavy rains received in the region last season.

a3181.speaker: Maureen Ndebele, project participant
a3181.name: Maureen Ndebele
a3181.title: project participant
a3181.speech: Said exporting to the European market is something their district desperately needs as it helps grow the local economy and the country at large: "Having a market in Europe means earning foreign currency, something our district desperately needs. These seeds are a God-given resource, and we are determined to make the most of this opportunity."

a3181.speaker: Fred Kutsiga, local business analyst
a3181.name: Fred Kutsiga
a3181.title: local business analyst
a3181.speech: Said the Matobo women's venture is an example of what's possible when rural communities are included into global value chains: "This success story is no longer just about survival of local women but it's about prosperity, pride, and the power of homegrown enterprise."

a3205.speaker: D. Nelson Bearngar, Director-General of the Center for National Documents and Records Agency (CNDRA)
a3205.name: D. Nelson Bearngar
a3205.title: Director-General of the Center for National Documents and Records Agency (CNDRA)
a3205.speech: Has called for increased financial support for the agency ; says the request is meant to improve the agency’s ability to preserve important national documents and records ; emphasized that the CNDRA is a revenue-generating institution for the Government of Liberia.

a3205.speaker: D. Nelson Bearngar, Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.name: D. Nelson Bearngar
a3205.title: Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.speech: Suggested that its employees deserve better pay to stay motivated ; stressed that adequately compensating employees of government ministries and agencies would help reduce corruption ; explained that poor wages could lead to unethical practices, asserting that top management should prioritize the welfare of employees and support the President’s agenda ; criticized leaders who indulge in luxuries while employees struggle to meet basic needs.

a3205.speaker: D. Nelson Bearngar, Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.name: D. Nelson Bearngar
a3205.title: Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.speech: Appealed to the government and its partners for additional support to make the agency more efficient in carrying out its responsibilities ; stated that preserving Liberia’s heritage requires a comprehensive approach and called on the government, development partners, and private individuals to assist in any way possible ; indicated that their assistance could be through financial contributions, materials, or technical support ; specifically reached out to international and regional partners, including the United States Government, USAID, UNDP, UNESCO, the African Union, ECOWAS, and others, to help mobilize the necessary resources for CNDRA.

a3205.speaker: D. Nelson Bearngar, Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.name: D. Nelson Bearngar
a3205.title: Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.speech: Clarified that the National Archives is more than just a place to obtain marriage certificates, as many people perceive it ; highlighted that the institution’s primary function is to manage and preserve Liberia’s documentary and cultural heritage to protect and honor the nation’s memories.

a3205.speaker: D. Nelson Bearngar, Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.name: D. Nelson Bearngar
a3205.title: Director-General of CNDRA
a3205.speech: Expressed gratitude to President Joseph N. Boakai for entrusting him with the responsibility to serve in his current role ; acknowledged the significant challenges the agency faces, many of which are still being addressed.

a3205.speaker: Liberian government, through the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning
a3205.name: Liberian government
a3205.title: through the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning
a3205.speech: Recently announced a salary increase for civil servants starting in January 2025.

a3265.speaker: Micheal Martin, Irish Foreign Minister
a3265.name: Micheal Martin
a3265.title: Irish Foreign Minister
a3265.speech: Said that while it was for the World Court to decide whether genocide is being committed, he wanted to be clear that Hamas' 7 October attack and what is happening in Gaza now "represents the blatant violation of international humanitarian law on a mass scale." ; "The taking of hostages. The purposeful withholding of humanitarian assistance to civilians. The targeting of civilians and of civilian infrastructure. The indiscriminate use of explosive weapons in populated areas. The use of civilian objects for military purposes. The collective punishment of an entire population," ; "The list goes on. It has to stop. The view of the international community is clear. Enough is enough."

a3265.speaker: Micheal Martin, Irish Foreign Minister
a3265.name: Micheal Martin
a3265.title: Irish Foreign Minister
a3265.speech: Did not say what form the intervention would take or outline any argument Ireland plans to advance, but added that the step was decided following legal and policy analysis and consultation with several partners including South Africa.

a3265.speaker: Irish Department of Foreign Affairs (Martin's department)
a3265.name: Irish Department of Foreign Affairs (Martin's department)
a3265.speech: Said such third party interventions do not take a specific side in the dispute, but that the intervention would be an opportunity for Ireland to put forward its interpretation of one or more of the provisions of the Genocide Convention at issue in the case.

a3265.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling, January
a3265.name: International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling
a3265.title: January
a3265.speech: Ordered Israel to refrain from any acts that could fall under the Genocide Convention and to ensure its troops commit no genocidal acts against Palestinians, after South Africa accused Israel of state-led genocide in Gaza.

a3265.speaker: Israeli tallies
a3265.name: Israeli tallies
a3265.speech: The Hamas-led attack killed 1 200 people and resulted in more than 250 being taken hostage.

a3265.speaker: Hamas-run health authorities in Gaza
a3265.name: Hamas-run health authorities in Gaza
a3265.speech: Israel's assault on Gaza has killed more than 32 000 people.

a3265.speaker: Israel (government)
a3265.name: Israel (government)
a3265.speech: Told the countries that their plan constituted a "prize for terrorism" that would reduce the chances of a negotiated resolution to the conflict between the neighbours.

a3291.speaker: Neale Richmond, Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.name: Neale Richmond
a3291.title: Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.speech: Emphasized that Ireland would not follow the international trend of cutting aid budgets: “We are absolutely committed to the multilateral process and the work of the United Nations and its agencies.” ; “While far too many countries are turning their backs on international development, Ireland has not cut its international development budget.” ; Reaffirmed that Ireland would remain steadfast, morally and financially, in supporting its global partners: “We will be there every step of the way. Where there are challenges, there are opportunities and we must rise to meet them.”

a3291.speaker: Neale Richmond, Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.name: Neale Richmond
a3291.title: Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.speech: Noted that Ireland has contributed USD$400 million to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria and pledged that this support would continue: “Ireland, of course, is a founding member of the Global Fund. We look forward to making our annual contribution later this year. That commitment will continue not just to the work of the Global Fund, but to many important partners working here in Zimbabwe.”

a3291.speaker: Neale Richmond, Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.name: Neale Richmond
a3291.title: Irish Minister of State at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
a3291.speech: Praised Zimbabwe for its efforts in combating malnutrition among children and urged other countries not to abandon development aid in the face of global financial pressures: “I challenge anyone who takes joy in cutting international development to visit the malnutrition ward here. Tell the parents that this is a budgetary measure, that there are other priorities. This is an investment, not an expense.”

a3291.speaker: Dr. Douglas Mombeshora, Zimbabwean Minister of Health and Child Care
a3291.name: Dr. Douglas Mombeshora
a3291.title: Zimbabwean Minister of Health and Child Care
