a3291.speech: Welcomed the reaffirmed support from Ireland, noting it would enable Zimbabwe to maintain key health programs: “Zimbabwe is among the top countries to achieve the 95-95-95 HIV targets. This has been made possible through collaboration with partners such as the Global Fund and the Government of Ireland.” ; “We’ve also reduced TB incidence by 20 percent. With continued support, we believe we can sustain this momentum.” Mombeshora further expressed optimism following recent assurances from both the Global Fund and the Irish government, stressing the importance of such partnerships in bolstering Zimbabwe’s healthcare delivery systems.

a3416.speaker: European Union (opinion piece, 'By the European Union')
a3416.name: European Union (opinion piece
a3416.title: 'By the European Union')
a3416.speech: Assures that the EU's partnership with Malawi is built to last: "Strong partnerships, however, are designed to withstand strong headwinds. And I can assure you that the EU's partnership with Malawi is built to last." ; "We do not intend to reduce our network across the globe. The EU has been present in Malawi for almost 40 years, and we are here to stay." ; "We want the EU in the world to be the antithesis to the autocratic axis forming today. To achieve that, we do not want to close offices, on the contrary, our plan is to grow Europe's reach."

a3416.speaker: European Union (opinion piece, 'By the European Union')
a3416.name: European Union (opinion piece
a3416.title: 'By the European Union')
a3416.speech: States that the EU and its Member States are still the largest global provider of Official Development Assistance, over 40% of the total amount, and that increasingly, when and where this money is spent, the EU "will make sure it reflects not only our values but the EU's interests, too."

a3416.speaker: European Union (opinion piece, 'By the European Union')
a3416.name: European Union (opinion piece
a3416.title: 'By the European Union')
a3416.speech: Says the EU will continue to be explicit and transparent about the strings attached to its cooperation "unlike some other global actors" - strings firmly attached to shared values: democracy, the rule of law, upholding human rights, sound management of public finances, accountability and transparency; and appreciates that Malawi continues to buck the trend by consistently voting against human, civil and sovereign rights violations and resisting pressure from autocracies.

a3416.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign and Security Policy
a3416.name: Kaja Kallas
a3416.title: EU High Representative for Foreign and Security Policy
a3416.speech: Clearly stated that multilateralism is under threat right now and that "we need to see this as an opportunity to develop the international system further, for it to be more inclusive for all countries in the world, and more accountable to their peoples." ; "We should be the architects of creative solutions."

a3691.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3691.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a3691.speech: According to the WHO, the arrival of the mosquito in Ethiopia triggered an “unprecedented increase” in the number of cases, which went from 4.1 million and 527 deaths last year to 7.3 million cases and 1,157 deaths between 1 January and 20 October 2024 ; according to the most recent WHO data, Africa accounted for 95% of the 244 million cases and 608,000 deaths due to malaria worldwide in 2022 ; barely a month ago the WHO declared Egypt free of malaria after more than a century of fighting the disease.

a3691.speaker: Meera Venkatesan, head of the malaria division at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3691.name: Meera Venkatesan
a3691.title: head of the malaria division at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3691.speech: “The invasion and spread of Anopheles stephensi can potentially upend the malaria landscape in Africa and undo decades of progress made in the fight against this disease.”

a3691.speaker: Meera Venkatesan, head of the malaria division at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3691.name: Meera Venkatesan
a3691.title: head of the malaria division at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a3691.speech: “The increased transmission caused by Stephensi could potentially help accelerate the spread of other threats.”

a3691.speaker: Study dating from 2020
a3691.name: Study dating from 2020
a3691.speech: According to a study dating from 2020, the mosquito could affect 126 million city dwellers across Africa.

a3691.speaker: Charles Mbogo, president of the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association
a3691.name: Charles Mbogo
a3691.title: president of the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association
a3691.speech: “We do not yet fully know the biology and behaviour of this mosquito” ; “It is possible that it is linked to the climate and that it needs high temperatures. Much more research is needed” ; said more funding must be mobilised to capture and study these mosquitoes and to raise public awareness of preventive measures, such as covering water containers.

a3691.speaker: Charles Mbogo, president of the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association
a3691.name: Charles Mbogo
a3691.title: president of the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association
a3691.speech: Said what is needed above all is “greater political will” ; “We share information as scientists with colleagues in neighbouring countries” ... “But we must reach a higher level.”

a3691.speaker: Dorothy Achu, head of tropical and vector-borne diseases in Africa at the WHO
a3691.name: Dorothy Achu
a3691.title: head of tropical and vector-borne diseases in Africa at the WHO
a3691.speech: “The arrival of (drug) resistance is imminent,” stressing that the WHO is working with the countries concerned to diversify treatment programmes and delay this phenomenon ; stressed that, faced with the lack of coordination between African governments, the WHO is working to develop “a more continental approach”.

a4101.speaker: Luís Morfin, Resident Deputy Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Mozambique
a4101.name: Luís Morfin
a4101.title: Resident Deputy Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Mozambique
a4101.speech: “Our partnership in the health sector has generated a multiplier effect of the U.S. government resources, which translates into greater capacity to offer high-quality public health services to families in Maputo province.”

a4101.speaker: Luís Morfin, Resident Deputy Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Mozambique
a4101.name: Luís Morfin
a4101.title: Resident Deputy Director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Mozambique
a4101.speech: Said the renovations created better conditions for privacy in consultation rooms, which are essential “for people to have confidence in their healthcare providers and for their right to health to be realized.”

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: Speaking at the opening ceremony for the Training of Interviewers for the 2024 Nigeria Verbal and Social Autopsy (VASA) Study in Akwanga, Nasarawa State, explained that key national agencies such as the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), National Primary Health Care Development Agency, Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, and the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs, are also part of the coordinating team.

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: Pointed out that understanding the factors behind maternal and child deaths is crucial to improving healthcare systems, policies and interventions: “This training marks an important milestone in our efforts to collect essential data on maternal and child health that will ultimately improve the lives of millions of Nigerians. Nigeria as a country, continues to face challenges in maternal and child health. Despite the progress we have made, preventable causes still claim the lives of our women and children. Understanding the factors behind these deaths is crucial to improving our healthcare systems, policies, and interventions.”

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: Explained that the 2024 VASA Study builds on the achievements of the 2014 and 2019 studies, which provided valuable insights into the causes of under-five deaths across the country, adding that this year’s study expands the scope to offer comprehensive data on both under-five and maternal deaths, contributing critical information that will guide decision-makers at both national and state levels.

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: Commending the collaboration among the agencies of government, said the exercise has demonstrated that collaboration is key to solving complex challenges like maternal and child mortality: “This collective effort underscores the importance of data-driven decision-making and highlights our shared commitment to improving health outcomes for Nigeria’s most vulnerable populations. We are also relying on the cooperation of state governments, particularly through the State Ministries of Health, to ensure that fieldwork proceeds smoothly. Effective partnerships at every level are essential to the success of this study, and I urge all stakeholders to remain fully engaged throughout the process.”

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: Charged fieldworkers, particularly interviewers, to approach the task with professionalism, empathy, and precision: “I urge you to approach this task with professionalism, empathy, and precision. You are not only collecting data; you are making a direct contribution to the health and well-being of millions of Nigerians. Your work must be guided by accuracy, integrity, and confidentiality. The information you gather will be used to shape policies and allocate resources where they are needed most. I encourage you to treat this responsibility with the seriousness it deserves, knowing that your efforts will help prevent further loss of life. Additionally, I emphasise the importance of maintaining ethical standards throughout your interactions. You will be dealing with families who may have experienced significant loss, and it is essential that you show respect, empathy, and confidentiality in all your engagements.”

a4227.speaker: Nasir Isa Kwarra, Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.name: Nasir Isa Kwarra
a4227.title: Chairman of the National Population Commission (NPC)
a4227.speech: In an interview with newsmen, underscored the need to improve the living conditions of Nigerians, adding that there is the urgent need to provide quality healthcare services to the citizenry; he appealed to the households where data collection would be conducted to cooperate with interviewers to ensure that accurate, reliable and quality data is collected for planning and development.

a4227.speaker: Prof. Alice Romokek Nte, Consultant Paediatrician at the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital
a4227.name: Prof. Alice Romokek Nte
a4227.title: Consultant Paediatrician at the University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital
a4227.speech: Said, based on the previous Demographic and Health Survey Reports, that Nigeria has not achieved the global health index; observed with dismay that maternal and child mortality continues to increase in Nigeria, attributing this ugly development to pervasive poverty, infections, malnutrition, teenage mothers and poor healthcare services in the country; and called on key stakeholders to redouble their efforts to bring down the causative factors for maternal and child deaths in the country.

a4227.speaker: Representative from the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
a4227.name: Representative from the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
a4227.speech: Advised the interviewers to be sensitive to the people’s culture, tradition and religion in the course of their data collection to achieve optimal result.

a4334.speaker: Press statement (China-Uganda Industrial Capacity Cooperation Exposition organisers)
a4334.name: Press statement (China-Uganda Industrial Capacity Cooperation Exposition organisers)
a4334.speech: "These series of China-Africa Expositions are one of the initiatives to further promote the implementation of the new measures of the Beijing Summit and build a platform for economic and trade cooperation between China and Africa." ; "The 2019 China-Uganda Expo has attracted 43 enterprises from 12 provinces and cities of China seeking to explore investment opportunities in Uganda in a wide range of industries including engineering, machinery, energy, equipment, agricultural processing products and equipment and automobiles."

a4334.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a4334.name: Xi Jinping
a4334.title: Chinese President
a4334.speech: Announced at the Beijing Summit for the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in September 2018 that China will launch "Eight Major Initiatives" together with Africa, draw a blueprint for the development of China-Africa relations in the new era, and open a grand chapter in China-Africa cooperation in the new era.

a4334.speaker: Yoweri Museveni, President of the Republic of Uganda
a4334.name: Yoweri Museveni
a4334.title: President of the Republic of Uganda
a4334.speech: Said during his recent visit at the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo in Changsha, Hunan Province: "In spite of the bottlenecks, the economy in Africa and that of Uganda has been growing fast. The future is good now, and in partnership with China, we will move fast, if we work together."

a4361.speaker: Brian Shukan, U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4361.name: Brian Shukan
a4361.title: U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4361.speech: Recalled that the partnership between his country and Benin is founded on shared values, notably a commitment to democracy, sustainable development, economic opportunity, security cooperation and the strengthening of ties between the two peoples ; “We appreciate our productive partnership with the government of President Patrice Talon to develop economic opportunities and the well-being of all Beninese.”

a4361.speaker: Brian Shukan, U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4361.name: Brian Shukan
a4361.title: U.S. Ambassador to Benin
a4361.speech: Cited as examples the achievements of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) since 2016, notably in access to land, justice and financial services, the modernization of the port of Cotonou, access to energy and the improvement of the Benin-Niger corridor whose compact was recently signed; also recalled the achievements of the United States Agency for International Development in the fight against malaria and tropical diseases, in improving maternal, neonatal and child health and family planning, and its work in water, sanitation and hygiene, good governance, human rights and social cohesion; and mentioned the work of Peace Corps volunteers in Benin over 55 years, the United States African Development Foundation, cooperation with the Beninese defence and security forces, the ambassador’s special self-help fund, and U.S.-sponsored professional and cultural exchange programmes.

a4361.speaker: Erick Jean-Marie Zinsou, Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a4361.name: Erick Jean-Marie Zinsou
a4361.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Benin
a4361.speech: Supported the ambassador’s remarks by recalling some of the achievements, actions and programmes of the United States in Benin, and conveyed the gratitude of the Beninese Executive to the American government and people; on the achievements of MCA-Benin II he reassured the American partner that arrangements have been made to ensure their sustainability; and on the regional compact he recalled that the modalities for finalizing the new compact are being completed in order ultimately to boost the Beninese economy.

a4410.speaker: Moumouni Boubacar Saidou, Nigerien Minister Delegate to the Prime Minister in charge of Finance
a4410.name: Moumouni Boubacar Saidou
a4410.title: Nigerien Minister Delegate to the Prime Minister in charge of Finance
a4410.speech: “We were dispatched to Bamako by His Excellency General Abdourahmane TIANI, President of the CNSP, to continue the discussions already engaged since last October with our Malian brothers on the harmonisation of our economic policies.” ; specified that this economic integration aims to correct certain anomalies in trade exchanges in order to optimise the economies ; “Within this framework, we held discussions for 48 hours with our Malian counterparts, and today we were received by His Excellency Army General Assimi GOITA to give him an account of our discussions and to gather his advice as well as his guidance.”

a4410.speaker: Assimi Goita, President of the Transition of Mali
a4410.name: Assimi Goita
a4410.title: President of the Transition of Mali
a4410.speech: Reassured his guests of his support and urged them to work actively for the construction of a confederal economy founded on endogenous economic development.

a4657.speaker: Prophet Sam Olu Alo, Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.name: Prophet Sam Olu Alo
a4657.title: Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.speech: has urged Nigerians to make sacrifices for others, stating that giving without expecting rewards opens doors to divine favour; he urged Nigerians to remember the less privileged and vulnerable members of society during this period and stressed the need for Muslims and Christians to engage in acts of charity and kindness, such as providing food and clothing to those in need.

a4657.speaker: Prophet Sam Olu Alo, Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.name: Prophet Sam Olu Alo
a4657.title: Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.speech: called on Muslims and Christians to use their respective fasting periods of Ramadan and Lent to pray for unity, peace, and progress in the country; noted (in a statement by his Personal Assistant Hon. Deji Ogunbusuyi) that prayer and fasting are essential tools for spiritual growth and development, and that Nigerians should utilize this time to seek divine intervention in the country’s challenges; said the collective prayer and fasting can bring about a sense of unity and purpose among Nigerians, and ultimately lead to a more peaceful and prosperous nation; reminded Muslims that Ramadan is a time for spiritual rejuvenation and self-reflection, urging them to strengthen their faith, seek forgiveness, and renew their commitment to Allah; called on Christians observing the 40-day Lenten period to use this time for introspection, self-reflection, and spiritual growth, and to pray for Nigeria, its leaders, and its people; called on Nigerians to pray for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abiodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State and other Nigerian leaders, saying the prayer was necessary to seek divine guidance and wisdom for the leaders as they navigate the country’s challenges.

a4657.speaker: Prophet Sam Olu Alo, Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.name: Prophet Sam Olu Alo
a4657.title: Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.speech: said the decision of the United States President Donald Trump to cut foreign aid to most African countries should not be seen as entirely negative, noting that while the move might seem unsettling, Trump was acting in his country’s best interest. “It may not be what we want to hear, but he is doing what is best for his nation. African leaders must also rise to do what is best for their own people,” he said. He therefore challenged African leaders to look inwards and develop strategies for self-sufficiency, reducing the continent’s reliance on foreign assistance.

a4657.speaker: Prophet Sam Olu Alo, Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.name: Prophet Sam Olu Alo
a4657.title: Planter of Christ Apostolic Church, Grace of Mercy Prayer Mountain World-wide
a4657.speech: Reading from Psalm 25:10, he urged Christians to keep God’s commandments, stressing that divine mercy plays a crucial role in human success. “When people lose the mercy of God, failure becomes inevitable,” he said, warning that pride, deceit and ingratitude often block people from receiving mercy.

a4880.speaker: Members of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs)
a4880.name: Members of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs)
a4880.speech: Are dismayed over the delisting of selected types of vehicles from duty-free privilege; the organisations claim the specific vehicles are necessary to deliver aid and humanitarian assistance in remote areas.

a4880.speaker: Ministry of Finance (directive, effective January)
a4880.name: Ministry of Finance (directive
a4880.title: effective January)
a4880.speech: The directive limits the types and numbers of vehicles investment projects are allowed to import tax-free, allowing investment projects to import minivans, minibuses, delivery vans and motor vehicles duty-free, while station wagons and pickup trucks are excluded from the list; it requires organisations to get approval documents from the authorities, register under the Civil Society Organization Authority, invoice and a bill of loading to enjoy the privilege of purchasing from local car importers.

a4880.speaker: Shimelis Gebeyehu, country representative director, Doctors of the World
a4880.name: Shimelis Gebeyehu
a4880.title: country representative director, Doctors of the World
a4880.speech: "We didn't import in order to save time."

a4880.speaker: Natae Ebba, lawyer in tax associate and corporate practice
a4880.name: Natae Ebba
a4880.title: lawyer in tax associate and corporate practice
a4880.speech: Said the vehicles were prohibited in the new investment regulation approved by the Council of Ministers in July 2022.

a4880.speaker: Natae Ebba, lawyer in tax associate and corporate practice
a4880.name: Natae Ebba
a4880.title: lawyer in tax associate and corporate practice
a4880.speech: Recommends the organisations urge the Ministry to reconsider through the Authority.

a4880.speaker: Henok Melese, director of the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council (ECSOC)
a4880.name: Henok Melese
a4880.title: director of the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council (ECSOC)
a4880.speech: According to Henok, further discussions are necessary, after officials from the Ministry discussed with the Authority and a dozen CSOs three weeks ago at Elilly International Hotel near ECA Road, Kazanchis.

a4880.speaker: Henok Melese, director of the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council (ECSOC)
a4880.name: Henok Melese
a4880.title: director of the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council (ECSOC)
a4880.speech: "Large spending on vehicles turns them into a luxury which is contrary to the organisations' visions," said Henok.

a4880.speaker: Seid Aman (PhD), country director of Imagine One Day
a4880.name: Seid Aman (PhD)
a4880.title: country director of Imagine One Day
a4880.speech: According to Seid, while securing funds from donors to purchase the vehicles is not easy, tax payments that may go up to 240pc beyond the actual price of the vehicles exacerbate the problem; "It's like adding fuel to the fire," he said.

a4880.speaker: Seid Aman (PhD), country director of Imagine One Day
a4880.name: Seid Aman (PhD)
a4880.title: country director of Imagine One Day
a4880.speech: He argues such kinds of laws should be tabled for discussions with the stakeholders rather than sudden enforcement.

a4880.speaker: Minilik Afework, digital marketer at Abyssina Car Sales
a4880.name: Minilik Afework
a4880.title: digital marketer at Abyssina Car Sales
a4880.speech: Is timid about the station wagon's capability to travel through difficult landscapes; however, he observes that customers prefer pickup trucks that frequent field duties due to their ground clearance while travelling through mud and heavy rocks.

a5067.speaker: Ferdinand Marcos Jr, Philippine President
a5067.name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr
a5067.title: Philippine President
a5067.speech: Suggested his country would be drawn into a potential conflict between China and the United States over Taiwan; during a state visit to India, said the Philippines' geographic proximity and the large Filipino community in Taiwan meant the country would be forced to get involved in the event of war ; "If there is an all-out war, then we will be drawn into it. There are many, many Filipino nationals in Taiwan and that would be immediately a humanitarian problem."

a5067.speaker: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a5067.name: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a5067.speech: Issued a strongly worded statement on Friday, warning Manila not to "play with fire" and urging it to uphold the one China principle ; "Geographical proximity and large overseas populations are not excuses for interfering in others' internal affairs." ; dismissed Marcos's justification as undermining both international law and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations charter, saying his comments risk destabilising regional peace and harming the interests of the Philippine people.

a5067.speaker: Philippine officials
a5067.name: Philippine officials
a5067.speech: Earlier this week condemned the launch of a Chinese rocket, which they said dropped suspected debris near a western province, alarming residents and threatening local ships and aircraft.

a5067.speaker: Washington (United States government)
a5067.name: Washington (United States government)
a5067.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to defend Filipino forces, including coastguard personnel, aircraft and public vessels, should they come under attack anywhere in the South China Sea.

a5068.speaker: Congressman Scott Perry, U.S. Subcommittee on Delivering Government Efficiency
a5068.name: Congressman Scott Perry
a5068.title: U.S. Subcommittee on Delivering Government Efficiency
a5068.speech: During a recent hearing, alleged that the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) had inadvertently funded terrorist organisations, including Boko Haram (BH), in Nigeria.

a5068.speaker: Alex Jones (post on X)
a5068.name: Alex Jones (post on X)
a5068.speech: On 13 February, a post claimed that an investigation by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) had compelled the US Congress to admit to a long-standing history of financing terrorist groups, including Boko Haram.

a5068.speaker: @adokwuandy (social media commentator on X)
a5068.name: @adokwuandy (social media commentator on X)
a5068.speech: "The 'farmer-herder' crisis in the Middle Belt and the bandit and BH crisis is beginning to make sense. All sponsored by USAID."

a5073.speaker: USAID (statement)
a5073.name: USAID (statement)
a5073.speech: Announced that all staff will be placed on administrative leave starting February 7 (Friday), including in Malawi; according to a statement released by USAID, the administrative leave is a precautionary measure aimed at ensuring the safety and security of all staff. The agency has not provided further details on the reasons behind this decision.

a5073.speaker: Development expert (anonymous)
a5073.name: Development expert (anonymous)
a5073.speech: "This is a surprise move, and we are not sure what it means for USAID's programs in Malawi... We hope that the agency will provide more information soon, so we can understand the implications of this decision."

a5090.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a5090.title: Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.speech: Has urged the ministry of health to formulate a clearly defined approach to guide the formulation of the annual health budget to achieve better health outcomes, emphasizing that a well-defined strategic framework would provide the ministry with a sustainable funding mechanism: "We need a policy direction based on a thorough situational analysis that addresses the prevailing health challenges" ; said the goal is not to jump from one initiative to another, but to identify root causes and address the problems at hand ; "Strategic planning and policy formulation are crucial", appealing to the ministry to develop a framework that supports annual budget increases.

a5090.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a5090.title: Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.speech: Said approximately 13% of the country's annual budget is dedicated to health services, stressing that there is need for increased investment to ensure the sustainability and effectiveness of health programmes, and that a targeted approach integrating budgets for key health issues such as HIV and tuberculosis is essential, with an estimated 15% of the budget allocated to these areas to maximise impact: "One of the key challenges facing health programmes is ensuring that funding supports critical interventions. These investments are vital to ensuring essential services are adequately funded and to protect citizens during crises." ; "For example, in upcoming budget debates, focus should be on tangible strategies and instruments that justify increased allocations, aiming to surpass the 15% threshold and ensure that health investments lead to real improvements in people's lives".

a5090.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a5090.title: Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.speech: Referenced recent regional meetings, including the Pan-African Health Summit, which highlighted progress in combating HIV, with treatment support reaching 3%, and TB control efforts achieving near 100% coverage, excluding second-line drug resistance cases such as multi-drug resistant (MDR) TB: "However, despite these successes, weaknesses remain in programme support mechanisms, particularly in areas like viral load testing and the availability of trained personnel."

a5090.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a5090.title: Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.speech: Said fluctuations in funding, changes in programme names and shifting priorities create instability that hampers long-term planning and service delivery: "The government must take full responsibility by prioritising domestic funding and strategic planning to safeguard health programmes from external uncertainties." ; "It is time for Lesotho to reduce reliance on foreign aid and focus on financing core health sector activities. By doing so, we would have safeguarded the country from potential collapse."

a5090.speaker: Mokhothu Makhalanyane, Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.name: Mokhothu Makhalanyane
a5090.title: Chairperson of the parliamentary Social Cluster Committee, Lesotho
a5090.speech: Highlighted the link between health and economic growth: "Without a healthy population, the economy cannot thrive, and critical workforce segments are at risk from non-communicable diseases. Health must remain a priority across all sectors, with government leadership ensuring that budgets are protected and efficiently utilised." ; stressed that the future of national health depends on strategic planning, increased domestic investment, and resilient mechanisms to support critical interventions.

a5141.speaker: Judge Carl Nichols, US federal judge appointed by President Trump
a5141.name: Judge Carl Nichols
a5141.title: US federal judge appointed by President Trump
a5141.speech: Ordered a temporary halt to the layoff plans affecting thousands of USAID employees, and also agreed to block another order that gave USAID staff based abroad 30 days to relocate to the United States with their families at the government's expense ; held that the two measures would have exposed American workers and their families to risks, logistical challenges and unjustified expenses.

a5168.speaker: Abass Ahmed, 34-year-old Somali refugee and teacher in Dadaab camp
a5168.name: Abass Ahmed
a5168.title: 34-year-old Somali refugee and teacher in Dadaab camp
a5168.speech: “I have lived in Dadaab for 30 years and this is the first time we have received no food assistance at all.” ; “It’s the worst ever that we have experienced.” ; said life has never been so tough as swingeing U.S. aid cuts finally bite; said his five-year-old son and seven-year-old daughter now frequently complain of nagging stomachs: “I try to distract them with play or by giving them some milk, if we have some, but it’s not easy.”

a5168.speaker: Abass Ahmed, 34-year-old Somali refugee and teacher in Dadaab camp
a5168.name: Abass Ahmed
a5168.title: 34-year-old Somali refugee and teacher in Dadaab camp
a5168.speech: Fears refugees like him are already forgotten: “We feel depressed and have so much anxiety. If the international community cannot help us, people will end up dying.”

a5168.speaker: Mercy Juma, head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.name: Mercy Juma
a5168.title: head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.speech: Said food assistance to refugees had been shrinking since 2018 due to funding shortfalls, with the most severe reductions implemented at the end of 2024 partly due to a lack of U.S. commitments. “The United States was our biggest donor, providing around 70% of our total budget, so the withdrawal of funding from the U.S. has had a serious impact on refugees in Kenya.” ; “People are already opting to eat one meal a day, mothers are eating less in order to feed their children, people are selling their belongings. When you reduce food, it will lead to a slow starvation.”

a5168.speaker: Mercy Juma, head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.name: Mercy Juma
a5168.title: head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.speech: Said WFP was now only able to provide food to 480,000 out of the 700,000 refugees it used to support in Kenya. “We are really worried about the long-term impacts of reduced rations,” adding that children were being taken out of school to work and there was a higher risk of malnutrition among children.

a5168.speaker: Mercy Juma, head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.name: Mercy Juma
a5168.title: head of communications for the World Food Programme (WFP) in Kenya
a5168.speech: Said WFP is appealing for $220 million to provide food to refugees for the next six months, but donors have only pledged $52 million so far.

a5168.speaker: United Nations
a5168.name: United Nations
a5168.speech: According to the United Nations, nearly 37 million people worldwide are refugees – with 69% from just five countries: Syria, Venezuela, Ukraine, Afghanistan and South Sudan.

a5168.speaker: Abass Issak, 45-year-old shopkeeper in Dadaab
a5168.name: Abass Issak
a5168.title: 45-year-old shopkeeper in Dadaab
a5168.speech: Said he was forced to close his small grocery store in July after 10 years of business, earning about $400 a month. “I went bankrupt. Customers had no money and bought food on credit, but they couldn’t pay me back. I was owed hundreds of dollars.” ; “Many shops like mine are collapsing.”

a5168.speaker: Government officials (Kenya)
a5168.name: Government officials (Kenya)
a5168.speech: Said an empty WFP store was torched by refugees who were angered by their slashed rations.

a5193.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), human rights group
a5193.name: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety)
a5193.title: human rights group
a5193.speech: Has raised alarm over alleged Fulani Jihadists plot to impose Sultanate in Nigeria by 2075.

a5193.speaker: Emeka Umeagbalasi, chairman of Intersociety, and other leaders of the group (special report)
a5193.name: Emeka Umeagbalasi
a5193.title: chairman of Intersociety, and other leaders of the group (special report)
a5193.speech: Said already Nigeria is headquartering 22 Islamic terror groups in Africa seeking to obliterate Christianity and indigenous cultural heritage to achieve this purpose with world Jihad fund.

a5193.speaker: Intersociety special report
a5193.name: Intersociety special report
a5193.speech: Stated that the terror groups, presently using Nigeria as their ‘safest haven’, are also seeking to obliterate or wipe out an estimated 112 million Christians and 13 million traditional religionists across the country, particularly in South-East and South-South by the year 2075 or in 50 years' time ; “The groups to achieve the objectives, had so far massacred 7,087 Christians and abducted 7,800 in 220 days of 2025, mostly Christians from South East, South South, who are either killed or incarcerated alongside thousands of liberal Muslims particularly across core Northern Muslim States dominated” ; “They have killed 185,009 defenseless Nigerians since 2009 (16 Years) including 125,009 Christians And 60,000 liberal Muslims during Which 19,100 churches were razed, and more than 1,100 Christian communities sacked” ; “20,000 square miles of their lands were taken-over and over 600 Christian clerics abducted including abduction of 250 Catholic priests and 350 pastors and killing of dozens. They have forced out estimated 12m-14m Christians out of their homes to become IDPs and millions of others fled” ; said the Islamic terror groups are using violence and genocidal means to obliterate or wipe out Nigeria's indigenous ethnic groups and their identities especially the 3,475-year-old Igbo cultural heritage put in place since 1450BC.

a5193.speaker: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), human rights group
a5193.name: International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety)
a5193.title: human rights group
a5193.speech: Believed that even the far-reaching punitive measures by US, EU, UK, and Canadian leaders were not only belated and long overdue, and that “all the first-class Fulani Muslims and top Islamic clerics and leaders, including those of the MACABAN, must be banned from traveling to these religious freedom compliant and respectful countries” ; also wants world leaders and respecters of human rights to review hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of annual humanitarian, democracy, military, and development assistance to Nigeria.

a5312.speaker: Zuma Kavirombo, principal development officer of the Namibia Horse Racing Association (NHRA)
a5312.name: Zuma Kavirombo
a5312.title: principal development officer of the Namibia Horse Racing Association (NHRA)
a5312.speech: Shared with New Era Sport that about 70 horses registered for the prestigious competition and will vie in 18 sprints: "This is one of the top events in the horseracing calendar. Various clubs want to close the year on a high note. We expect a huge turnout at Gobabis at this event." ; He added that the NHRA is developing amid sponsorship challenges, and the racing clubs are tuning their clubs by adding new horses: "This is amazing, and we are expecting four or more new juvenile horses which will make the debut at the Gobabis competition."

a5312.speaker: Katjauana Muriambihu of the Omaheke Supporters Club
a5312.name: Katjauana Muriambihu of the Omaheke Supporters Club
a5312.speech: Said his prime aim is to keep the main trophy in the Omaheke region.

a5312.speaker: Zuma Kavirombo, principal development officer of the Namibia Horse Racing Association (NHRA)
a5312.name: Zuma Kavirombo
a5312.title: principal development officer of the Namibia Horse Racing Association (NHRA)
a5312.speech: Said it shows that horseracing is growing, and horse owners are putting more emphasis in their horses to compete at the highest level ; confirmed that there will be live performances from the One Blood music group between intervals.

a5420.speaker: Addis Abeba city officials
a5420.name: Addis Abeba city officials
a5420.speech: Argue the edict banning the use of hotel venues for government meetings is designed to tighten fiscal discipline as Addis Abeba shoulders the weight of its record-high 350 billion Br budget for the 2025/26 fiscal year, the first financed entirely from internal revenue without federal subsidies ; claim that renovations to in-house facilities, public halls and office cafeterias will prove cheaper than hotel fees in the long run.

a5420.speaker: Yoseph Tale, deputy head of the Addis Abeba City Finance Bureau
a5420.name: Yoseph Tale
a5420.title: deputy head of the Addis Abeba City Finance Bureau
a5420.speech: “We can’t afford wasteful spending when our priority is investment.” ; “If their meeting rooms or cafeterias are not in good condition, they are encouraged to renovate them.”

a5420.speaker: Mehariw Temesgen, public relations director, City Youth & Sports Bureau
a5420.name: Mehariw Temesgen
a5420.title: public relations director, City Youth & Sports Bureau
a5420.speech: “We already have alternative halls available,” citing venues such as Adwa Museum and Africa Convention Centre for larger gatherings.

a5420.speaker: Zenash Ketema, deputy head of the Women, Children & Social Affairs Bureau
a5420.name: Zenash Ketema
a5420.title: deputy head of the Women, Children & Social Affairs Bureau
a5420.speech: Said the facility only holds 20, while typical training sessions draw upwards of 200 participants: “With this restriction, we cannot train such a large group at once in our office. Since hotels are no longer an option, we'll have to depend on borrowing conference rooms from other bureaus, which will make our work more challenging. We'll be requesting exemptions for key events to avoid bottlenecks in operations.”

a5420.speaker: Gadisa Girma, managing director of Haile Resorts & Hotels
a5420.name: Gadisa Girma
a5420.title: managing director of Haile Resorts & Hotels
a5420.speech: Called the ban overzealous: “It’s reasonable to save public funds, but not by completely prohibiting hotels,” advocating for a calibrated policy that allows large-scale trainings and conferences to continue in hotels ; “The city might save in one pocket but lose even more in another through reduced tax revenue.”

a5420.speaker: Fitteh Woldesenbet (PhD), president of the Ethiopian Hotel & Tourism Employers Federation
a5420.name: Fitteh Woldesenbet (PhD)
a5420.title: president of the Ethiopian Hotel & Tourism Employers Federation
a5420.speech: “The government is the single largest client for hotels. If it stops booking events, what will hotels do?” ; said removing this source of revenue would not only hurt hotels but also undermine government tax collection.

a5420.speaker: Mustofa Abdella, CEO of Zafer Plus Consultancy
a5420.name: Mustofa Abdella
a5420.title: CEO of Zafer Plus Consultancy
a5420.speech: Sees the policy as potentially self-defeating; warned that with donor-funded programs shrinking, private demand tepid, and now government bookings halted, the city Administration’s decision will compress profit margins, intensify competition for corporate clients, and potentially lead to job cuts and business closures: “This is a perfect storm.” ; urged the Administration to implement restrictions on the number of events city bureaus hold in hotels gradually or, at the very least, allow discounted, essential-use exceptions: “Without such measures, the city risks eroding its own tax base and discouraging investment.”

a5420.speaker: Atlaw Alemu (PhD), economics lecturer at Addis Abeba University
a5420.name: Atlaw Alemu (PhD)
a5420.title: economics lecturer at Addis Abeba University
a5420.speech: “When businesses are frustrated and uncertain, they lose motivation.” ; said budget targets cannot be met at the expense of private sector viability, especially in employment-rich sectors like hospitality, and called for a rebalancing of priorities, urging city officials to invest not simply in roads and parks but also in healthcare, education, and cost-of-living relief: “People are struggling with food, not fountains. Creating sustainable jobs will expand the city’s revenue base more reliably than austerity alone.”

a5487.speaker: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC), Investigative Report on the Violence & Human Rights Violations following Musician Hachalu Hundessa's Assassination (2020)
a5487.name: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC)
a5487.title: Investigative Report on the Violence & Human Rights Violations following Musician Hachalu Hundessa's Assassination (2020)
a5487.speech: Recommends: "To media and activists/social media influencers. To recognize there is an increasing vulnerability to atrocity crimes and taking into consideration the current complex ethnic, religious and political tensions in the country, to avoid sharing/producing content that, directly or indirectly, promotes discrimination, suspicion and hatred thereby aggravating the risk for violent conflicts."

a5487.speaker: Norwegian Nobel Committee
a5487.name: Norwegian Nobel Committee
a5487.speech: Awarded President Obama the 2009 Nobel Peace Prize "for his extraordinary efforts to strengthen international diplomacy and cooperation between peoples" ; awarded the Prime Minister of the FDRE the prize "for his efforts to achieve peace and international cooperation, and in particular for his decisive initiative to resolve the border conflict with neighbouring Eritrea."

a5487.speaker: Barack Obama, former US President (in his book A Promised Land, 2020, p. 499)
a5487.name: Barack Obama
a5487.title: former US President (in his book A Promised Land, 2020, p. 499)
a5487.speech: "I couldn't help but think about the daily fighting that continued to consume Iraq and Afghanistan and all the cruelty and suffering and injustice that my administration had barely even begun to deal with. The idea that I, or any one person, could bring order to such chaos seemed laughable."

a5487.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia (Nobel lecture, 2019)
a5487.name: Abiy Ahmed
a5487.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia (Nobel lecture, 2019)
a5487.speech: "(I)t is estimated that some 70 percent of Africa's population is under the age of 30. Our young men and women are crying out for social and economic justice. They demand equality of opportunity and an end to organized corruption. The youth insist on good governance based on accountability and transparency. If we deny our youth justice, they will reject peace. Standing on this world stage today, I would like to call upon all my fellow Ethiopians to join hands and help build a country that offers equal justice, equal rights, and equal opportunities for all its citizens" ; extended his arms to the international community to join Ethiopia's efforts of building enduring peace and prosperity in the Horn of Africa.

a5487.speaker: Farouk El-Baz, Egyptian scientist (interview, 2019)
a5487.name: Farouk El-Baz
a5487.title: Egyptian scientist (interview, 2019)
a5487.speech: "It is a matter of ignorance on our part because Ethiopia is the place where the rain falls and comes through Sudan to us. It is the source of the Nile River. Our grandfathers and grandmothers learned about this and made good relationships with Ethiopia and Sudan. We have forgotten that, especially in the last fifty years. We forgot that we are a partner of African countries."

a5487.speaker: A study in The Netherlands (migration studies)
a5487.name: A study in The Netherlands (migration studies)
a5487.speech: Indicated more and more migrants are taking the role of get-kippers: a Moroccan migrant in the Netherlands today is more likely to discourage a friend or family member from moving to Europe, to shield their loved ones from far-right rhetoric.

a5487.speaker: Hillary Clinton (2016)
a5487.name: Hillary Clinton (2016)
a5487.speech: "You could put half of Trump's supporters into what I call the basket of deplorables. Right? The racist, sexist, homophobic, xenophobic, Islamaphobic - you name it. And unfortunately, there are people like that. And he has lifted them up. He has given voice to their websites that used to only have 11,000 people -now how 11 million. The other half feel that the government has let them down and desperate for change. Those are people we have to understand and empathize with as well."

a5528.speaker: Writer of the Reporter “Ene Emlew” column article “Will ethnic-based federalism take us far?”
a5528.name: Writer of the Reporter “Ene Emlew” column article “Will ethnic-based federalism take us far?”
a5528.speech: As the writer I cited in my introduction said, we must be careful that the hardening of ethnic politics does not end in disintegration ; as the writer I mentioned at the outset said, now not only in each region but in each zone and district, ethnic politicians, analysts and activists are being hatched in droves, clinging to the identity agenda as alpha and omega.

a5528.speaker: Political scientists (scholars of political science)
a5528.name: Political scientists (scholars of political science)
a5528.speech: Say that the real causes of the failure to listen to one another as a country, of the struggles of ethnic and religious extremism, and of the killing in conflict and civil war, are the breakdown of the system and the narrowing of the democratic space, rather than poverty.

a5528.speaker: Studies cited on Nigeria’s federalism
a5528.name: Studies cited on Nigeria’s federalism
a5528.speech: There are studies saying that Nigeria, which is said to have an earlier experience of federalism, found relief only after changing the form and content of its system, once identity-based demarcation had cost it dearly.

a5528.speaker: Ethiopian government (statement at government level)
a5528.name: Ethiopian government (statement at government level)
a5528.speech: In earlier years it kept being said at government level, “our aim is to inflame Amhara nationalism.”

a5528.speaker: Negede Abiy, author of the opinion article
a5528.name: Negede Abiy
a5528.title: author of the opinion article
a5528.speech: Says he shares the cited writer’s worry and wishes to set out his personal fear that the stretching and hardening of ethnic politics may, beyond party squabbling, aggravate the civil war and plunge the country into unending crisis ; argues that the main national challenge now facing the country is the ethnic narrative and ethnic confrontation creating mistrust among peoples, that founding an ethnic party has become a lucrative business, and that tearing apart through ethnic politics the interaction of peoples who have lived bound together for ages is “a crime worse than crime” ; concludes that a systemic reform that cools the hardening of ethnic politics and brings multi-ethnic unity must be created through the peace efforts and the national dialogue commission, otherwise preventing the mutual killing will not be as easy as imagined.

a5528.speaker: Ethiopian Reporter (Editor’s note)
a5528.name: Ethiopian Reporter (Editor’s note)
a5528.speech: “We state that the article reflects only the writer’s own view.”

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: Motivating the budget in Parliament on Tuesday, said the ministry needs N$11.5 billion for medical supplies, including clinical services, prioritising the replacement of outdated equipment and expansion of specialities, and that despite global disruptions the ministry is actively implementing multiple strategies to enhance the pharmaceutical supply chain, including establishing a dedicated procurement mechanism to streamline the sustainable supply of medicines and clinical items over five years, reducing shortages and enhancing transparency ; “Data systems will enhance annual quantification and quality data-collection methods to achieve an 80% service level target through electronic inventory systems like the Electronic Dispensing Tool, Stock Cards and Pharmaceutical Dashboard.”

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: Said the ministry’s planned activities encompass upgrading the Central Medical Stores’ (CMS) logistics and storage capacity to achieve an 80% service level – up from 57% – involving procuring new CMS storage infrastructure, enhanced logistics systems, and robust inventory management; and requested the allocation of N$62.5 million to further refine health data and policy support, including detailed epidemiological analysis and research, prioritising the review of the National Electronic Health Strategy (2021–2025) to advance work on a TeleHealth Policy.

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: Requested the allocation of N$114.4 million to cover HIV/AIDS-related expenses ; “Namibia has been lauded for making great progress towards achieving the UNAIDS 95-95-95 global targets, with 93% of all people living with HIV (PLHIV) aware of their status; 95% of those aware of their status being on antiretroviral treatment (ART); and 98% of those on ART virally suppressed. Above 90 % of persons receiving ART have transitioned to the more efficacious Dolutegravir Regimen.”

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: “Although funding cuts have raised concerns about access to antiretroviral medications, I wish to clarify that the government of Namibia has been procuring these medicines since 2016, and will continue to do so. Recent waivers issued by the United States’ (US) government to Namibia have allowed some continued support under the US-CDC [Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Cooperative] Agreement with the ministry, although USAID-funded activities have been suspended. These supported activities relate mainly to HIV and tuberculosis prevention programmes.”

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: Said the ministry will prioritise the construction and upgrading of critical health infrastructure, including nine new clinics and two health centres in remote areas such as Onamukulo, Uuvudhiya and Oranjemund ; “Upgrades at major hospitals, including Gobabis, Swakopmund, Katutura and St. Mary’s will expand capacity, modernise facilities and improve patient care standards. The development of a new Windhoek District Hospital through a project financing facility by the Ministry of Finance is underway this year to decongest urban health facilities and improve access.”

a5582.speaker: Dr Esperance Luvindao, Namibian Health Minister
a5582.name: Dr Esperance Luvindao
a5582.title: Namibian Health Minister
a5582.speech: Said filling remaining vacant posts, especially specialists, with emphasis on underserved areas by allocating N$150 million in this budget, is essential for strengthening Namibia’s healthcare capacity ; “The ongoing deployment and development of a pool of technical specialists in paediatrics, obstetrics, surgery, internal medicine, anaesthesiology and critical care will enhance service accessibility and quality across the country. The full implementation of the Integrated Human Resources Information System (IHRIS) will continue to optimise workforce planning, deployment and performance management.”

a5582.speaker: Penda Ithindi, Namibian health executive director (statement)
a5582.name: Penda Ithindi
a5582.title: Namibian health executive director (statement)
a5582.speech: Issued a statement refuting reports of the unavailability of anaesthetic pharmaceuticals in various public health facilities, assuring that adequate levels of stock of anaesthetics are available at most health facilities, including Windhoek Central Hospital, Katutura Intermediate Hospital and Keetmanshoop District Hospital, and that the low levels are not due to the absence of anaesthetics ; “The observed low stock at Rundu Intermediate Hospital is mainly due to weak coordination and active monitoring between the different functional units and Central Medical Stores, resulting in untimely distribution and delivery of the supply orders. Noting the observed low stock situation at Rundu Intermediate Hospital, the ministry has instituted immediate measures to ensure that an adequate quantity of requisite stock is dispatched to the Rundu Intermediate Hospital.”

a5582.speaker: Penda Ithindi, Namibian health executive director
a5582.name: Penda Ithindi
a5582.title: Namibian health executive director
a5582.speech: Said the ministry has put in place a pharmaceutical supply and distribution strategy underpinned by forward-looking, timely procurement activity, digital monitoring mechanisms between the Central Medical Store and the regional health facilities, as well as stock accountability provisions across the value chains for efficiency and effectiveness.

a5604.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a5604.name: Antonio Guterres
a5604.title: UN Secretary-General
a5604.speech: Before the Fifth Committee of the General Assembly on Friday 17 October 2025, issued an urgent appeal: "if member states do not quickly regularise their contributions, the UN could find itself in a situation of bankruptcy" ; denounces a critical situation in which "credit returns" and budgetary arrears compromise the organisation's operational capacity.

a5604.speaker: Former Malian diplomat (anonymous), expert on the UN system
a5604.name: Former Malian diplomat (anonymous)
a5604.title: expert on the UN system
a5604.speech: "This is not just a cash-flow crisis. It is the very model of multilateral financing that is faltering. The great powers hesitate to support an institution they consider too normative. But weakening the UN means weakening global dialogue, solidarity and conflict prevention."

a5652.speaker: US State Department
a5652.name: US State Department
a5652.speech: Froze almost all foreign assistance worldwide, with immediate effect, including for Mozambique; the measure does not apply to humanitarian programmes, and excludes resources destined for Israel and Egypt.

a5652.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a5652.name: Donald Trump
a5652.title: US President (executive order)
a5652.speech: Determines that: “All heads of departments and agencies with responsibility for United States foreign development assistance programmes must immediately halt new obligations and disbursements of development assistance funds to foreign countries and implementing non-governmental organisations, international organisations and contractors, pending reviews of such programmes for programmatic efficiency and consistency with United States foreign policy, to be conducted within 90 days of this order.”

a5652.speaker: Trump administration
a5652.name: Trump administration
a5652.speech: Warns that “it is the policy of the United States that no further United States foreign assistance shall be disbursed in a manner that is not fully aligned with the foreign policy of the President of the United States.”

a5669.speaker: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (communiqué)
a5669.name: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (communiqué)
a5669.speech: According to the communiqué, the suspension of USAID funds is justified by the same arguments brandished by Donald Trump’s supporters, namely presumptions of covert financing of terrorism; the transition authorities, according to the same communiqué, even claim an anticipatory posture on the matter, with a purported refusal to grant the no-objection notice to the funding of all USAID projects that were reluctant to pass through the state channel.

a5761.speaker: Government of Burundi
a5761.name: Government of Burundi
a5761.speech: According to the Burundian government, the project aims to enhance market linkages to regional and international hubs, boosting the global competitiveness of Burundian products

a5761.speaker: Marie Chantal Nijimbere, Minister of Trade, Transport, Industry, and Tourism of Burundi
a5761.name: Marie Chantal Nijimbere
a5761.title: Minister of Trade, Transport, Industry, and Tourism of Burundi
a5761.speech: Said the project aligns with the Government of Burundi’s national development priorities, supporting the country’s vision for socio-economic growth by enhancing trade, economic diversification, and job creation, and emphasised the need for such initiatives to improve market access for local producers: “One of the major barriers our producers, especially micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), face is limited market access due to inadequate technology, investment, and non-compliance with production standards. These challenges affect the competitiveness of ‘Made in Burundi’ products in regional and international markets. The UGUSHORA project will address these issues by facilitating trade, building exporters’ capacity, and improving the competitiveness of Burundian products, unlocking new market opportunities.”

a5761.speaker: Ted Hunink, Deputy Head of Mission and Head of Cooperation at the Netherlands Embassy
a5761.name: Ted Hunink
a5761.title: Deputy Head of Mission and Head of Cooperation at the Netherlands Embassy
a5761.speech: Emphasized the project’s significance in enhancing trade and export opportunities for targeted enterprises in Burundi: “UGUSHORA, meaning ‘to export,’ is a direct response to the call made by the Burundian Government during the investors’ roundtable in December 2024. This initiative reinforces the Netherlands’ commitment to supporting Burundi’s economic objectives while strengthening its position in regional and global markets.”

a5761.speaker: Christian Nibasumba, TradeMark Africa’s Burundi Country Representative
a5761.name: Christian Nibasumba
a5761.title: TradeMark Africa’s Burundi Country Representative
a5761.speech: “By empowering MSMEs through trade facilitation and capacity building, UGUSHORA will create jobs, boost incomes, and improve livelihoods in Burundi.”

a6010.speaker: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) (statement)
a6010.name: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) (statement)
a6010.speech: Announced the suspension of its activities in the Zamzam camp and warned in a statement that the camp, near El Fasher, was attacked on 11 and 12 February, worsening an already catastrophic humanitarian situation ; "The current escalation of attacks and fighting in and around the Zamzam camp makes it impossible for MSF to continue providing medical assistance in such dangerous conditions."

a6010.speaker: Yahya Kalilah, MSF head of mission in Sudan
a6010.name: Yahya Kalilah
a6010.title: MSF head of mission in Sudan
a6010.speech: "Eleven patients died at the MSF hospital, including five children, because we could not treat them properly or transfer them to the Saudi hospital, the only facility with surgical capacity near El Fasher." ; "In January and in December, two of our ambulances transporting patients from the camp to El Fasher were shot at. Today the situation is even more dangerous and many people, including patients requiring trauma surgery or an emergency caesarean section, are trapped in Zamzam."

a6010.speaker: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6010.name: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6010.speech: Reports that access to water and food is becoming increasingly precarious and that the central market was looted and burned down, depriving residents of essential resources.

a6010.speaker: Yahya Kalilah, MSF head of mission in Sudan
a6010.name: Yahya Kalilah
a6010.title: MSF head of mission in Sudan
a6010.speech: "Stopping our project while the disaster worsens in Zamzam is a heartbreaking decision. For more than two years, our teams have done their best to provide care against all odds, despite the siege, supply shortages and many other challenges." ; "However, as the battle of El Fasher rages and now reaches the Zamzam camp directly, the most minimal security conditions are currently not in place for us to remain." ; Says the proximity of the violence, the great difficulty in sending supplies, the impossibility of sending experienced staff to provide adequate support and the uncertainty about exit routes from the camp for MSF colleagues and civilians leave the organisation with little choice.

a6010.speaker: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6010.name: Doctors Without Borders / Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF)
a6010.speech: Denounces humanitarian inaction and calls for immediate intervention; urges all parties to the conflict to respect civilian populations and to allow those who wish to flee to do so safely; recalls the need to scale up humanitarian aid where this remains possible; argues that the warring parties must guarantee unhindered access to aid and that their allies and influential states must use their influence to remove the obstacles that are causing deaths and famine ; Says it is continuing its emergency operations in Tawila and other parts of Darfur while awaiting a possible resumption of activities in Zamzam.

a6063.speaker: Leulseged Tadese Abebe, career senior diplomat (author)
a6063.name: Leulseged Tadese Abebe
a6063.title: career senior diplomat (author)
a6063.speech: writes that a common, implementable continental strategy ought to be drawn to ensure that African countries once again do not become pawns but active players that assert their own interests.

a6063.speaker: Antonio Guterres, United Nations Secretary-General
a6063.name: Antonio Guterres
a6063.title: United Nations Secretary-General
a6063.speech: “The Cold War is back with a vengeance,” he said ; a month ago, Guterres warned that we are living in a “more dangerous place now than during the Cold War” between the Americans and the Soviets.

a6063.speaker: US Census Bureau (data)
a6063.name: US Census Bureau (data)
a6063.speech: According to the US Census Bureau, in 2021 the total US-Africa trade volume was 64.2 billion dollars.

a6063.speaker: Chinese Customs Agency (data)
a6063.name: Chinese Customs Agency (data)
a6063.speech: According to the Chinese Customs Agency, in 2021 China’s trade volume with Africa was valued at a record high of 254 billion dollars.

a6101.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6101.name: Marco Rubio
a6101.title: US Secretary of State
a6101.speech: Said: "We are redirecting our foreign aid programmes so that they align directly with the interests of the United States and its citizens."

a6101.speaker: US State Department (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the United States)
a6101.name: US State Department (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the United States)
a6101.speech: Informed Congress that it will take over some of USAID's responsibilities as part of an operational restructuring, and that programmes which do not meet the priorities of the Trump administration will be cancelled.

a6101.speaker: Dr Seif Shekalaghe, Permanent Secretary of Tanzania's Ministry of Health
a6101.name: Dr Seif Shekalaghe
a6101.title: Permanent Secretary of Tanzania's Ministry of Health
a6101.speech: Said the halting of the aid means nothing will be done differently, because the government has a duty to serve citizens and no service will falter: "USAID made its contribution but it was not 100 per cent, they were assisting the government. To date all the stakeholders we work with are contributing. Even when they leave, the government continues to deliver. They came in and helped; we will carry on as usual serving citizens." ; Asked about the departure of health workers who had been paid by organisations receiving USAID funds, he said: "We have not yet received any report that services have failed to be delivered; work is going on as usual." ; Said the government has been working in collaboration with both external and domestic stakeholders.

a6101.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister of Finance of Tanzania
a6101.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a6101.title: Minister of Finance of Tanzania
a6101.speech: Said, when presenting the 2025/2026 national budget proposals to parliament on 12 June 2025, that the measures follow ongoing global policy changes which have caused key development partners to reduce the aid they provided for health services, including the fight against diseases, particularly HIV/AIDS; said the government proposes to establish alternative revenue sources to reduce the budget deficit caused by the decline in that aid by amending various laws: "It is proposed that 70 per cent of the additional revenue be channelled to the AIDS Trust Fund (ATF) and 30 per cent to the National Health Insurance Fund for All" ; listed amendments to the Excise Duty Act, CAP 147 to raise excise on alcoholic drinks (Sh20 per litre on beer, Sh30 per litre on wine, Sh50 per litre on spirits), to raise excise on electronic communication services from 17 to 17.5 per cent, and new levies on fuel, minerals, gambling, casino games, and imported vehicles and machinery, including Sh250,000 per machine for excavators, bulldozers and fork lifts: "Also to charge Sh500 on every ticket issued by a rail transport service provider and Sh1,000 on every ticket issued by an air transport service provider."

a6101.speaker: Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6101.name: Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6101.speech: Said the government should look at how to increase human resources in the areas from which those workers have left.

a6101.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT) and surgical specialist at Benjamin Mkapa Hospital
a6101.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a6101.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT) and surgical specialist at Benjamin Mkapa Hospital
a6101.speech: Said: "Citizens still want services. The closure of the agency does indeed have direct effects. First, it was sudden; second, we were not used to it. Now many have lost their jobs. This will not last forever, we will stand again, though I do not know for how long." ; Said they are advising the government to see how it can intervene so that services continue to be provided at the facilities that had been set aside ; Said that even with the United States withdrawing, Tanzanians still need services including HIV/AIDS care, infectious diseases, vaccination and nutrition services: "Those services were essential, they do not change. Because America has withdrawn, our people still need services. We saw the government establish eight revenue sources to address HIV and other health services, including Health Insurance for All." ; "We do not want this to be a short-term thing. This is a wake-up bell: he who depends on his brother's property dies poor. We must look at how we move on from where we are. And in the government's plans it is not that all doors are closed; we can look at other foreign organisations we can work with."

a6101.speaker: Dr Elisha Osati, health consultant and expert
a6101.name: Dr Elisha Osati
a6101.title: health consultant and expert
a6101.speech: Said the United States has made a large contribution to many institutions and organisations in the country working on education, health and the environment, and that the American withdrawal awakens us to self-reliance; stressed that the country must organise itself: "We need to strengthen ourselves greatly internally. We have the ATF fund but we have never directed effort to that area. Also, on our African continent we should be able to persuade major nations such as China to invest a lot of money in the WHO."

a6101.speaker: New study published in the journal The Lancet / the researchers
a6101.name: New study published in the journal The Lancet / the researchers
a6101.speech: Details how the gains made over the past two decades in reducing child and adult deaths could collapse following the closure of USAID, with the 132 countries that benefited directly from USAID funding at risk of losing a total of 14 million people by 2030; the researchers said: "Our estimates show that, if the funding cuts announced and implemented in the first half of 2025 are not reversed, a large number of avoidable deaths could occur by 2030."

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Warned Wednesday that the world is on a “dark and dangerous path” as rising nationalism and fragmented responses to global crises threaten the rules-based international order, calling instead for renewed international solidarity to confront existential threats ; said member states were straying from the UN’s founding principles of peace, security, and development: “Eighty years on since the first UN General Assembly, we should have already been better together, not seeking to justify why we cannot be better together today.” “Instead of asking what is right under international law, we are witnessing the unapologetic rise of national might to settle disputes.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Cited worsening conditions for fragile states, noting that more than 30 UN members, including Somalia, face instability driven by conflict, weak institutions, and climate change ; pointed to food insecurity as a growing crisis, saying the World Food Program estimates 319 million people in 67 countries face acute hunger: “These stark and startling facts must give us all pause for reflection” ; urged nations to redouble efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030: “If we as a community of nations are serious about progress, we must strengthen multilateralism, solidarity, and shared action.”

a6160.speaker: World Food Program (estimate cited)
a6160.name: World Food Program (estimate cited)
a6160.speech: Estimates 319 million people in 67 countries face acute hunger.

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Highlighted his country’s work as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council, pledging to advance peace and stability beyond its borders: “We are actively working with all Security Council members to find solutions for peace in the Middle East, Africa, and Europe.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Called for urgent action to ease Palestinian suffering: “The ongoing violence, displacement, and deprivation in the occupied territories, including Gaza, demand our collective conscience and urgent action” ; urged “an immediate and lasting ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, and renewed commitment toward the two-state solution.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Said the country is preparing to hold its first universal suffrage election in 57 years, part of broader reforms to consolidate democracy and stability: “Somalia was Africa’s first democratic nation in the 1960s, and we are proudly returning to that path of inclusive governance once again.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Credited Somali security forces and community defence groups for their fight against al-Shabaab and ISIS, saying their sacrifices have “made our people and citizens across the world safer” ; vowed operations would continue “until we achieve complete victory and harmony in our country, our region, our continent, and the wider world.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Warned that climate change is worsening fragility in developing nations like Somalia, which contributes “almost nothing” to global emissions but endures some of the harshest consequences; droughts, floods, and displacement, he said, are eroding livelihoods and reversing hard-won gains: “For us, climate change is not an abstract. It is a horrible reality of disrupted and destroyed lives.”

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Said Somalia is building on recent debt relief reforms by raising domestic revenue and tightening financial controls; noted that Somalia has joined the East African Community, is ratifying African Continental Free Trade Area policies, and is advancing World Trade Organization membership.

a6160.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6160.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6160.title: President of Somalia
a6160.speech: Closed his address by framing Somalia as both a country rebuilding from decades of conflict and a partner ready to contribute to global peace and development: “When we all work in unison, we are truly better together. No nation can stand alone in the face of threats that respect no frontiers.”

a6271.speaker: Leaders around the world, from US President Donald Trump to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni
a6271.name: Leaders around the world
a6271.title: from US President Donald Trump to Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni
a6271.speech: Have appreciated India’s timely assistance against a merciless pandemic.

a6271.speaker: Vladimir Norov, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Secretary-General
a6271.name: Vladimir Norov
a6271.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Secretary-General
a6271.speech: Observed that India is playing the role as the pharmacy of the world during the Covid-19 pandemic with its vast experience and deep knowledge in medicine, setting the tone for many regional and global initiatives.

a6271.speaker: Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India
a6271.name: Narendra Modi
a6271.title: Prime Minister of India
a6271.speech: Hosted a virtual conference of the leaders of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and pledged $10 million SAARC Emergency Fund to combat the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) in the region; at the first virtual G20 summit, underlined the imperative for a new kind of humane globalization, which goes beyond economic and financial calculations.

a6271.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6271.name: Donald Trump
a6271.title: US President
